item.title: Anthony Chen’s ‘We Are All Strangers’ to Bring 57th IFFI to a Poignant Close
item.description: Ministry of Information & Broadcasting Anthony Chen’s ‘We Are All Strangers’ to Bring 57th IFFI to a Poignant Close We Are All Strangers: A Tender Exploration of Love, Family and the Bonds That Transcend Generations; received critical aclaim and great reception at the International Film Festivals at Berlin, Melbourne, and Helsinki in 2026 Posted On: 19 NOV 2026 3:26PM by PIB Mumbai Goa, 19 November 2026 The 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) will draw its curtains with ‘ We Are All Strangers’ , a compelling feature film by acclaimed…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Information & Broadcasting
Anthony Chen’s ‘We Are All Strangers’ to Bring 57th IFFI to a Poignant Close
We Are All Strangers: A Tender Exploration of Love, Family and the Bonds That Transcend Generations; received critical aclaim and great reception at the International Film Festivals at Berlin, Melbourne, and Helsinki in 2026
Posted On: 19 NOV 2026 3:26PM by PIB Mumbai

Goa, 19 November 2026

 

The 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) will draw its curtains with ‘We Are All Strangers’, a compelling feature film by acclaimed Singaporean filmmaker Anthony Chen. A 2026 Singaporean production, the film will be screened as the festival’s Closing Film, offering audiences an evocative cinematic exploration of human relationships, familial ties and the complexities of contemporary life.

Set against the textured backdrop of contemporary Singapore, We Are All Strangers centres on 21-year-old Junyang, whose carefree existence is upended when a sudden turn in his relationship compels him and his girlfriend to confront the weight of adulthood far sooner than imagined. Simultaneously, the arrival of a spirited woman in the life of Junyang’s hardworking father subtly alters the unspoken equilibrium between father and son. Anchored by compelling performances, the film interlaces these parallel journeys as both generations navigate love, loss, and accountability, redefining the contours of family and the delicate ties between the kin we inherit and the people we choose.

We Are All Strangers marks the latest chapter in Anthony Chen’s celebrated ‘Growing Up’ trilogy, extending the empathetic, acutely observed storytelling that first won him the Cannes Caméra d’Or for his debut, Ilo Ilo (2013), and continued through Wet Season. Prior to its showcase in Goa, the film was presented at the 2026 Berlin International Film Festival and garnered acclaim at the Melbourne and Helsinki International Film Festivals.

The 57th IFFI, organised by the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, Government of India, and the National Film Development Corporation (NFDC), in association with the Entertainment Society of Goa (ESG), will be held in Panaji from 20th to 28th November 2026. The festival will be celebrated under the theme ‘Stories Without Borders’, bringing together diverse cinematic voices and stories from across the world.

 

* * *

PIB IFFI Team | Rajith Chandran/ Lekshmi Priya S S/ Swadhin Shakti Prasad/ Darshana Rane | IFFI 57 - 31

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Defence
Media registration opens for Aero India 2027
Posted On: 19 NOV 2026 3:10PM by PIB Delhi

The registration for media personnel for Aero India 2027 has commenced. This 16th edition of Asia’s largest air show and one of the world’s premier aerospace & defence exhibitions is scheduled to be held at Air Force Station, Yelahanka in Bengaluru, Karnataka from February 8 to 12, 2027. The mediapersons who are interested in covering the event can register on https://aeroindia.gov.in/. The registration will close on January 4, 2027.

For the registration, applicants must have the following:

  • PIB or State accreditation card for accredited journalists and a valid media identity card for non-accredited mediapersons. (File size not exceeding 1 MB)
  • Government-issued photo identity card for all media personnel. (File size not exceeding 1 MB)
  • A recent self-photograph. (File size not exceeding 512 KB)
  • A valid ‘J’ visa for foreign journalists. (File size not exceeding 1 MB)

Organised by the Department of Defence Production, Ministry of Defence, Aero India 2027 will serve as a major global platform bringing together leading aerospace and defence companies, policymakers, technology experts, innovators, industry representatives and defence personnel. The five-day event will feature an extensive exhibition alongside a series of business and strategic engagements, facilitating industry collaborations, government-industry interactions, technology demonstrations and knowledge exchange. A major highlight will be the spectacular aerial displays by the Indian Air Force and participating international flying teams, showcasing cutting-edge aviation technologies and capabilities.

The 16th Aero India is expected to further strengthen India’s commitment to Aatmanirbhar Bharat and reinforce its position as a reliable partner in the global aerospace & defence supply chain. The event will provide a major platform for Indian defence industries, including MSMEs and start-ups, to showcase their capabilities, explore new business opportunities and forge partnerships, while fostering investments, exports and technology collaborations.

item.content:encoded:
PIB Backgrounder
India’s Electronics Exports Gain Momentum
Non-Smartphone Products Emerge as a Strong Growth Engine
Posted On: 19 NOV 2026 3:01PM by PIB Delhi

India’s electronic goods exports grew by 44% to US$ 31.97 billion during April-September 2026-27. Smartphones remained the largest export segment, with shipments rising 35.8% to US$   18.17 billion. Non-smartphone electronics recorded faster growth of 56.5%, reaching $13.79 billion and increasing their share of total electronics exports to 43.2%. Key products included printed circuit boards, network transmission equipment, memory integrated circuits and storage devices. Strong export growth across these segments, with markets including Singapore, China, Hong Kong and Malaysia, reflects the broadening of India’s electronics export basket and growing presence in global markets.

 

Electronics Exports Register Strong Growth

India’s electronic goods exports continued to demonstrate strong momentum during April-September 2026-27, rising 44.0% from US$ 22.20 billion to US$ 31.97 billion. While smartphones remained the largest component of the electronics export basket, the period witnessed significantly faster growth in non-smartphone electronics. This indicates a broadening of India’s electronics export base across components, circuit boards, communication equipment, memory products and storage devices.

Non-Smartphone Electronics Drive Export Diversification

A particularly strong story emerged from the non-smartphone electronics segment, where exports increased by 56.5%, from US$ 8.81 billion to US$ 13.79 billion. Consequently, the segment’s share in India’s total electronic goods exports increased from 39.7% to 43.2%, reflecting an increasingly diversified electronics export basket.

The expansion was supported by sharp gains across several key commodities.

Parts and Accessories- Mounted Printed Circuit Boards

Exports surged from US$ 63.3 million to US$ 2.10 billion, growing by 3219%, with Singapore emerging as the dominant destination at US$ 1.87 billion, followed by China at US$ 111.5 million.

Populated, Loaded or Stuffed Printed Circuit Boards

Exports also expanded strongly, increasing from US$ 213.7 million to US$ 864.1 million, growing by 304%. China was the leading market at US$ 789.2 million, while exports to Hong Kong increased from US$ 5.9 million to US$ 25.3 million.

Network Transmission and Routing Equipment

Exports nearly doubled from US$ 732.9 million to US$ 1.45 billion, growing by 98%. The increase was led by Hong Kong, where exports rose from US$ 264.7 million to US$ 857.7 million. The United States and the Netherlands were also important markets at US$ 130.9 million and US$ 124.4 million, respectively.

Memory Integrated Circuits

Exports witnessed particularly rapid expansion, rising from just US$ 23.1 million to US$ 562.4 million, growing by 2333%. Malaysia emerged as the largest destination at US$ 390.8 million, followed by Singapore at US$ 102.4 million and Hong Kong at US$ 25.2 million.

Solid-State Non-Volatile Storage Devices

Exports increased sharply from US$ 14.6 million to US$ 260.5 million, growing by 1680%. China led the growth with exports reaching US$ 108.6 million. This was followed by Singapore at US$ 76.8 million, Hong Kong at US$ 22.3 million and the United States at US$ 20.7 million.

 

Smartphone Exports Rise

India’s exports of smartphones increased from US$ 13.38 billion in April- September 2025-26 to US$ 18.17 billion in April- September 2026-27, registering strong growth of 35.8%.

Smartphones continued to account for the majority of India’s electronic goods exports, although their share moderated from 60.3% to 56.8%. This moderation came amid even stronger growth in other segments of the electronics export basket.

Strengthening India’s Position in Global Electronics Trade

Taken together, the trends point to a broader and increasingly diversified electronics export basket. Smartphones continue to provide a strong foundation, with exports reaching US$ 18.17 billion, while non-smartphone electronics are expanding at a faster pace and increasing their contribution to overall electronics exports.

The sharp growth across printed circuit boards, communication equipment, memories and solid-state storage devices, alongside expansion into markets such as Singapore, China, Hong Kong and Malaysia, highlights the growing contribution of non-smartphone products to India’s electronics export momentum.

Reference

Ministry of Commerce and Industry

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Road Transport & Highways
NHAI Clarifies Vehicle Insurance Renewal SMS Alerts Are Part of Awareness Initiative; No Challans or Penalties at Toll Plazas
Proposed initiative is purely informational, aimed at encouraging timely renewal and responsible vehicle ownership
Posted On: 19 NOV 2026 2:58PM by PIB Delhi

National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) would like to clarify that SMS notifications currently being received by select National Highway users regarding vehicle insurance renewal are part of an ongoing testing process for a proposed public awareness initiative.

NHAI emphasizes that the initiative is purely informational and advisory in nature. There is no provision for issuing challans or imposing any penalties at toll plazas in connection with these alerts. Highway users are assured that the SMS system is not linked to any enforcement or punitive action at toll plazas. The notifications are intended simply to alert vehicle owners about the upcoming expiry dates of their motor insurance policies, encouraging timely renewal to ensure continuous coverage.

By facilitating advance reminders, NHAI aims to promote responsible vehicle ownership and support compliance with statutory road safety requirements through awareness. Through such initiatives, NHAI remains committed to encouraging safe road-user behaviour and strengthening the broader road safety ecosystem.

item.dc:creator: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
item.description: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change Union Environment Minister directs Delhi-NCR Civic Bodies to adopt Zero-tolerance Approach towards Air Pollution Violations; Calls for Strict Penal Action against Defaulters Daily Monitoring, Accountability of Ward-level Officials and Time-bound Enforcement of Pollution Control Measures to be Prioritised: Shri Bhupender Yadav Posted On: 19 NOV 2026 2:10PM by PIB Delhi Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change (EFCC), Shri Bhupender Yadav, today chaired a review meeting virtually from…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
Union Environment Minister directs Delhi-NCR Civic Bodies to adopt Zero-tolerance Approach towards Air Pollution Violations; Calls for Strict Penal Action against Defaulters
Daily Monitoring, Accountability of Ward-level Officials and Time-bound Enforcement of Pollution Control Measures to be Prioritised: Shri Bhupender Yadav
Posted On: 19 NOV 2026 2:10PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change (EFCC), Shri Bhupender Yadav, today chaired a review meeting virtually from Antalya (Türkiye), with the civic bodies of Delhi, Ghaziabad, Noida, Gurugram and Faridabad to assess preparedness and implementation of their Winter Action Plans for control of air pollution in Delhi-NCR. Emphasising that the current winter period demands visible and sustained action on the ground, the Minister requested the concerned public representatives and officials to ensure strict enforcement, daily monitoring and clear accountability at every level. He stressed that governance should increasingly be citizen-centric and facilitative, while ensuring that citizens are not subjected to unnecessary panic while taking pollution control measures.

The meeting was attended by Union Minister of State (MoEFCC), Shri Kirti Vardhan Singh; Secretary (MoEFCC), Shri Narendra Bhooshan; Chairperson (CAQM), Shri Rajesh Verma; Secretary (Department of Capital Development, MoHUA), Smt. D. Thara; Director General and Special Secretary (MoEFCC), Shri Santosh Tewari; Additional Secretary (MoEFCC) and Chairperson (CPCB), Dr. Amandeep Garg; Mayors and Commissioners of the respective Municipal Corporations, along with CEO Noida Authority and senior officials of respective State Governments. Shri Tarun Pithode, Member Secretary, CAQM, presented the progress made by respective NCR cities, while the Chairperson, CAQM, gave an overview of the on-ground implementation of their action plans and measures yet to be taken on different fronts.

Taking a strong stance against violations, Shri Yadav directed Municipal Corporations to adopt a zero-tolerance approach towards open burning of municipal waste, dry leaves and biomass, and ensure prompt penal action against violators. He called for operationalising Quick Response Teams in every ward to respond to complaints within hours, and fixing accountability of concerned officers for enforcement failures. He also called for immediate corrective measures for complete processing daily waste generated and time-bound accelerated legacy waste remediation, particularly at Bhalswa and Okhla dumpsites. Stressing the need for coordinated and decentralised governance, the Minister called for regular ward-level reviews by Mayors and dedicated WhatsApp groups with designated nodal officers for time-bound grievance redressal. He urged civic bodies to learn from and replicate successful initiatives across NCR, including MC Delhi's Malba App, MC Faridabad's Pothole Ambulance, MC Gurugram's survey-based identification of sanitation workers and Ghaziabad Nagar Nigam's shareable Construction and Demolition (C&D) waste portal.

On road dust management, Shri Yadav directed civic bodies to expedite road repairs, augment the capacity of Mechanical Road Sweeping Machines (MRSMs) on a war footing and ensure their full utilisation, including double-shift operations during winter. He called for GPS-enabled monitoring, ICCC-based supervision and daily removal of roadside dust, silt and construction debris. The Minister also stressed the need for advance planning of road development and dust mitigation measures in Gurugram, including greening of identified open spaces to address PM10 pollution. He directed strict compliance with dust mitigation norms at C&D sites, operationalisation of wheel-washing facilities and regular inspections, with stringent enforcement action, including closure of seriously non-compliant sites. The objective, he emphasised, must be to ensure 'No Visible Dust' in and around construction sites. The Minister further called for ensuring enhanced awareness about Solid Waste Management Rules, with proactive identification of bulk waste generators, as demonstrated by Delhi.

Reviewing hotspot mitigation and GRAP implementation, Shri Yadav directed civic bodies to assign dedicated nodal officers and prepare hotspot-specific action plans, which should be regularly reviewed by Mayors and the designated officers. He called for strict implementation of all measures applicable under the prevailing stage of GRAP, without exception. Emphasising institutional accountability, the Minister directed Collectors to regularly review the performance of municipalities and take corrective action against lagging bodies. He further called upon the Secretaries of MoEFCC and MoHUA, besides Chairpersons of the CAQM and CPCB, to review the performance of respective Municipal Corporations and municipalities across NCR cities to ensure effective implementation of the directions on the ground.

Stressing that accountability must translate into measurable outcomes, the Minister requested the concerned officials to monitor public grievances in real time and close complaints only after physical verification and resolution. He also called for intensive public awareness campaigns involving concerned stakeholders. Emphasising the need for sustained efforts throughout the winter season, Shri Yadav said every ward must demonstrate visible action every day, backed by strict enforcement, continuous monitoring, citizen participation and accountability.

item.content:encoded:
Prime Minister's Office
Prime Minister meets Their Royal Highnesses The Prince and Princess of Wales
Prime Minister appreciates the Earthshot Prize's efforts to promote innovative solutions to global environmental challenges
They also exchange views on further strengthening the India-UK Comprehensive Strategic Partnership
Posted On: 18 NOV 2026 9:02PM by PIB Delhi

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi met Their Royal Highnesses The Prince and Princess of Wales in New Delhi on 18 November 2026.

Prime Minister welcomed the growing momentum in India-UK bilateral relations, guided by India-UK Vision 2035 and strengthened by the entry into force of the India-UK Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) in July 2026.

Prime Minister commended the work of the Earthshot Prize in encouraging innovative solutions to pressing environmental challenges. He appreciated its recognition of Indian innovators and their contributions to addressing global environmental challenges, including at the Earthshot Prize Awards held in Mumbai on 17 November 2026.

The meeting also provided an opportunity to exchange views on further strengthening the India-UK Comprehensive Strategic Partnership, including cooperation in defense, health, education, fin-tech and people-to-people ties.

Prime Minister also conveyed his warm regards to His Majesty King Charles III and to Prime Minister Andy Burnham.

item.title: India calls for an Open, Transparent and Equitable Second Global Stocktake under Paris Agreement; Presses for Accountability on Climate Finance and Technology Transfer, at COP31 in Antalya (Türkiye)
item.category: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
item.dc:creator: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
item.description: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change India calls for an Open, Transparent and Equitable Second Global Stocktake under Paris Agreement; Presses for Accountability on Climate Finance and Technology Transfer, at COP31 in Antalya (Türkiye) GST-2 must take Comprehensive View of Climate Action, recognise Implementation Gaps and deliver Solution-oriented Outcomes: Shri Bhupender Yadav Posted On: 18 NOV 2026 8:14PM by PIB Delhi Antalya (Türkiye), 18th November, 2026 Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Shri Bhupender…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
India calls for an Open, Transparent and Equitable Second Global Stocktake under Paris Agreement; Presses for Accountability on Climate Finance and Technology Transfer, at COP31 in Antalya (Türkiye)
GST-2 must take Comprehensive View of Climate Action, recognise Implementation Gaps and deliver Solution-oriented Outcomes: Shri Bhupender Yadav
Posted On: 18 NOV 2026 8:14PM by PIB Delhi

Antalya (Türkiye), 18th November, 2026

Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Shri Bhupender Yadav, has called for the Second Global Stocktake (GST-2) under the Paris Agreement to be an open, transparent and inclusive process, grounded in the best available science and equity, and delivering balanced outcomes across all aspects of climate action.

Addressing the High-Level Event on the Second Global Stocktake at UNFCCC COP31 in Antalya, Türkiye, the Minister said that the GST must take a comprehensive 360-degree view of the Paris Agreement and its implementation, taking stock of both achievements and existing gaps. He emphasised that the process must be guided by the principles of equity, Common but Differentiated Responsibilities and Respective Capabilities (CBDR-RC), with developed countries taking the lead in the light of national circumstances.

Shri Yadav highlighted that the Second GST provides an opportunity to assess progress across key areas, including updated Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs), Biennial Transparency Reports, international cooperation under Article 6, the Global Goal on Adaptation and the Just Transition Mechanism. He also stressed the importance of recognising scientific assessments and reports, particularly those emerging from developing countries, alongside IPCC reports.

The Minister emphasised that the GST-2 must examine why, despite progress in climate action, the world remains at risk of crossing the 1.5°C warming threshold in the coming years. He called for solution-oriented outcomes that guide Parties in updating their NDCs and address gaps in the means of implementation, particularly climate finance and technology transfer. He underlined that actual delivery in these areas has fallen far below the obligations and responsibilities of developed countries.

Concluding his address, Shri Yadav expressed India's expectation that the Second Global Stocktake would be conducted successfully and provide a balanced assessment of global climate action and implementation.

item.content:encoded:
Lok Sabha Secretariat
LOK SABHA SPEAKER PARTICIPATES IN VISHWA SHANTI MAHAYAGYA AT HISTORIC SHRI HATKESHWAR MAHADEV TEMPLE IN VADNAGAR
VADNAGAR STANDS AS AN ENDURING SYMBOL OF SPIRITUAL HERITAGE, DETERMINATION, AND SELFLESS PUBLIC SERVICE: LOK SABHA SPEAKER
PRIME MINISTER SHRI MODI’S JOURNEY FROM MODEST ROOTS IN VADNAGAR TO NATIONAL LEADERSHIP EXEMPLIFIES DEDICATION TO PUBLIC SERVICE: LOK SABHA SPEAKER
LOK SABHA SPEAKER INTERACTS WITH STUDENTS AND VISITS HISTORIC SCHOOLS, ARCHAEOLOGICAL EXPERIENTIAL MUSEUM, AND MUSEUM OF MUSIC IN VADNAGAR
Posted On: 18 NOV 2026 7:56PM by PIB Delhi

 Lok Sabha Speaker Shri Om Birla visited Vadnagar in Mehsana district, Gujarat, today and participated in a series of spiritual, educational, and cultural engagements.

Beginning his visit at the historic Shri Hatkeshwar Mahadev Temple, Shri Birla offered prayers and participated in the ongoing 10-day Vishwa Shanti Mahayagya organised under the divine guidance and presence of Kanchi Kamakoti Peethadhipati Jagadguru Sri Shankara Vijayendra Saraswati Swamigal.

Sharing his reflections after the Mahayagya, the Lok Sabha Speaker described the ancient Hatkeshwar Mahadev Temple as a sacred centre of India’s spiritual heritage that inspires generations. He noted that the Vishwa Shanti Mahayagya and Havan, held under the leadership of Jagadguru Shankaracharya Ji, are dedicated to universal peace, harmony among nations, and the welfare of all humanity and living beings.

Highlighting the significance of Vadnagar as a sacred centre of India’s cultural legacy and the birthplace of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, Shri Birla remarked that the historic town stands as an enduring symbol of spiritual heritage, determination, and selfless public service. He said that visiting the town and seeing the Prime Minister’s school and the places associated with his formative years offer deep insight into how extraordinary resolve can triumph over adversity. He observed that the town serves as an inspirational landmark demonstrating that regardless of economic hardship, family struggles, or challenging circumstances, clear goals and unwavering determination enable an individual to achieve their aspirations.

Shri Birla noted that from his early student days, Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s life has been defined by a spirit of learning, dialogue, debate, and spiritual inspiration drawn from the ideals of Swami Vivekananda. Driven by the resolve of Seva (service), he left home at a young age to travel across the country, understanding India’s diverse social and economic realities firsthand. Calling this journey a testament to the strength of Indian democracy, the Speaker said that rising from a small town amidst modest circumstances to lead the nation exemplifies how dedication to public service shapes leadership.

Underscoring the Prime Minister’s milestone of 25 years of continuous public service as Chief Minister and Prime Minister, Shri Birla said that this enduring commitment serves as a major source of inspiration for every citizen. Having personally experienced economic and social challenges early in life, the Prime Minister has channelled those insights into building a self-reliant (Atmanirbhar) and self-sustaining India capable of overcoming future challenges, the Speaker added.

Following his engagements at the temple, the Lok Sabha Speaker visited Prerna School in Vadnagar, where he interacted warmly with students, encouraging them to cultivate curiosity, engage in constructive dialogue, and dedicate themselves to nation-building. He also visited Shri B.N. High School, paying tribute to the educational institutions that shaped young minds in the historic town.

Later, Shri Birla visited the Archaeological Experiential Museum and the Museum of Music in Vadnagar, appreciating the rich civilisational, archaeological, and musical legacy of one of India’s oldest living towns.

 

गुजरात प्रवास के दौरान वडनगर स्थित प्रेरणा स्कूल का भ्रमण करने का अवसर मिला। यह वही ऐतिहासिक विद्यालय है, जहाँ आदरणीय प्रधानमंत्री श्री @NarendraModi जी ने अपने विद्यार्थी जीवन के महत्वपूर्ण वर्ष बिताए और अपनी प्रारंभिक शिक्षा प्राप्त की। विद्यालय में अध्ययनरत विद्यार्थियों के साथ संवाद कर उनके विचारों, सपनों और आकांक्षाओं को जानने का अवसर मिला। युवा पीढ़ी की ऊर्जा, प्रतिभा और संकल्प ही विकसित भारत के निर्माण की सबसे बड़ी शक्ति हैं। आज के विद्यार्थी ही कल राष्ट्र की दिशा और दशा तय करेंगे। उनका ज्ञान, चरित्र, संस्कार और नवाचार के प्रति दृष्टिकोण भारत के उज्ज्वल भविष्य की आधारशिला बनेगा। इस विद्यालय से जुड़ी स्मृतियों, संघर्षों और जीवन-मूल्यों के प्रसंगों ने प्रधानमंत्री जी की प्रेरणादायी जीवन-यात्रा के प्रारंभिक पड़ावों को और निकट से जानने-समझने का अवसर दिया। निश्चय ही, जीवन की बड़ी यात्राओं की नींव ऐसे ही अनुभवों, संस्कारों और दृढ़ संकल्पों में निहित होती है।

— Om Birla (@ombirlakota) November 18, 2026

 

समानो मन्त्रः समितिः समानी, समानं मनः सह चित्तमेषाम्। समानं मन्त्रमभिमंत्रये वः, समानेन वो हविषा जुहोमि ।। गुजरात के वडनगर स्थित ऐतिहासिक श्री हाटकेश्वर महादेव मंदिर में आयोजित विश्व शांति महायज्ञ में जगद्गुरु श्री शंकर विजयेंद्र सरस्वती स्वामीगल के दिव्य सान्निध्य एवं मार्गदर्शन में सम्मिलित होकर आध्यात्मिक अनुभूति प्राप्त हुई। वैदिक मंत्रोच्चार, यज्ञ की पावन आहुतियों और प्रार्थनाओं के मध्य विश्व शांति, सामाजिक सद्भाव, मानव कल्याण एवं समस्त सृष्टि के मंगल की कामना की। हमारी सनातन संस्कृति का शाश्वत संदेश “सर्वे भवन्तु सुखिनः” संपूर्ण विश्व के सुख, शांति और कल्याण की भावना को अभिव्यक्त करता है। प्रार्थना है कि सनातन संस्कृति की यह आध्यात्मिक चेतना मानवता को सदैव सद्भाव, करुणा और शांति के पथ पर प्रेरित करती रहे।

— Om Birla (@ombirlakota) November 18, 2026

 

***

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
Vice President of India Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan Addresses 8th Convocation of VMMC & Safdarjung Hospital in the Presence of Union Health Minister Shri J.P. Nadda
A Medical Degree Is Not Merely an Academic Qualification, but a Lifelong Commitment to Humanity: Vice President of India Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan
Doctors Are the Most Respected Citizens of the Country: Vice President
A Medical Profession Is a Privilege That Comes with a Profound Responsibility Towards Society: Union Health Minister J.P. Nadda
Union Health Minister J.P. Nadda Highlights India's Remarkable Expansion in Medical Education Under the Leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi
Government Committed to Adding 75,000 Medical Seats by 2029: Union Health Minister
423 students receive degrees; 46 meritorious students awarded medals as institution marks 25 years of excellence in medical education and healthcare
Posted On: 18 NOV 2026 7:54PM by PIB Delhi

Vice-President of India, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, addressed the 8th Convocation Ceremony of Vardhman Mahavir Medical College (VMMC) and Safdarjung Hospital, New Delhi, today, in the presence of Union Minister of Health and Family Welfare, Shri J. P. Nadda. The convocation was organised as part of the institution’s Silver Jubilee Year celebrations, marking 25 years of its establishment (2001–2026).

Addressing the gathering, Vice President, Shri C.P. Radhakrishnan, the Hon’ble Vice President of India, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, congratulated Vardhman Mahavir Medical College (VMMC) and Safdarjung Hospital on completing 25 years of dedicated service in medical education and healthcare delivery. He observed that the institution continues to serve as a vital pillar of the country’s public healthcare system, making significant contributions to medical education, patient care and the development of healthcare professionals. Highlighting the progress made in the healthcare sector under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, he noted that the country has witnessed substantial expansion of its healthcare infrastructure, including the establishment of 12 new AIIMS over the past 12 years.

Reflecting on the responsibilities that accompany the medical profession, the Vice President emphasised that a medical degree is not merely an academic qualification but a lifelong commitment to humanity. He reminded the graduating students that despite remarkable advancements in medical science and technology, the human touch and compassionate relationship between a doctor and a patient remain irreplaceable. He urged them to uphold the highest standards of professional ethics and ensure that every patient is treated with dignity, compassion and respect, irrespective of their financial circumstances or social background. He underscored that there must be no discrimination in the delivery of healthcare and that every individual deserves equal and humane treatment.

Referring to the national vision articulated by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, the Vice President highlighted the goal of building a Viksit Bharat by 2047. He observed that the vision of a developed India cannot be realised without a healthy India, making a strong and equitable healthcare system indispensable to the country's overall development. He called upon the graduating doctors to recognise their important role in advancing this national aspiration through their professional commitment and service to society.

Addressing the young graduates, the Vice President observed that among the country's 140 crore citizens, doctors occupy a uniquely respected position because of the trust and responsibility associated with their profession. He encouraged them to regard this respect as both a privilege and a responsibility, always placing the nation above personal considerations and remaining committed to the welfare of society. He also urged the graduating students to say no to drugs, promote awareness against substance abuse and actively encourage others to lead healthy and responsible lives.

Speaking at the Occasion, Shri J.P. Nadda, described the occasion as a momentous milestone, symbolising years of dedication, academic excellence and commitment to service. Congratulating the students on successfully completing their medical education, he observed that graduating from Vardhman Mahavir Medical College was a matter of great distinction, given the exceptional clinical exposure, diverse learning opportunities and professional experience that the institution offers. He emphasised that while education is a fundamental right, the opportunity to enter the medical profession is a privilege that entails a profound responsibility towards society. He urged the graduates to discharge this responsibility with dedication, compassion and integrity, and to place their professional knowledge and skills at the service of humanity.

Highlighting the remarkable transformation of India's medical education landscape under the visionary leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, Shri Nadda noted that the country has made significant strides in expanding both medical education infrastructure and institutional capacity. He observed that India, which had only one AIIMS by the end of the 20th century, now has 23 AIIMS. Similarly, the number of medical colleges has increased from 387 to 863, with plans to establish 75,000 additional medical colleges over the next five years.

Referring to the Prime Minister's announcement from the ramparts of the Red Fort regarding the expansion of medical education capacity, Shri Nadda reiterated the Government's commitment to creating 75,000 additional medical seats. He expressed confidence that this target would be realised by 2029. Underscoring the scale of expansion achieved over the past decade, he stated that undergraduate medical seats have increased from approximately 51,000 to 1.43 lakh, while postgraduate seats have risen from around 31,000 to 91,000.

Emphasising that the expansion of medical education has been accompanied by an equally strong focus on maintaining academic and institutional standards, Shri Nadda stated that the Government remains committed to ensuring that increased capacity does not come at the cost of quality. He further informed that the Union Cabinet, in December 2025, approved financial assistance of ₹1.5 crore for each additional undergraduate and postgraduate medical seat, with an overall allocation of ₹15,000 crore to facilitate the creation of 10,000 additional medical seats.

Concluding his address, Shri Nadda reminded the graduating students that their achievements were not solely the outcome of their individual efforts but also reflected the sacrifices, encouragement and support of their parents, families and the larger society. He urged them to remain conscious of this collective contribution and to give back to society through selfless service, professional excellence and a steadfast commitment to their responsibilities as healthcare professionals.

Welcoming the Dignitaries, Dr. Kavita Rani Sharma, Director, VMMC & Safdarjung Hospital, extended her gratitude to the dignitaries and highlighted the institution’s remarkable journey of 25 years in medical education and healthcare delivery. She described the institution as a representation of the harmonious integration of medical science and healthcare, with education and service continuing to remain at the core of its institutional ethos. Emphasising the values that define the medical profession, she urged the graduating students to uphold the highest standards of integrity, honesty and ethical conduct, and to discharge their professional responsibilities with dedication, compassion and a strong commitment to patient care.

During the ceremony, the Hon’ble Vice President of India, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, released the Annual Report and Silver Jubilee Commemorative Volume of VMMC & Safdarjung Hospital. Furthermore, Vice President Shri C.P. Radhakrishnan led the pledge on “No to Drugs”, reinforcing the message of a drug-free society.

This was followed by the presentation of the Academic Report by Dr. (Prof.) Geetika Khanna, Principal, VMMC & Safdarjung Hospital, highlighting the institution’s achievements and progress in medical education, healthcare delivery and research.

A total of 423 students received their degrees during the ceremony, including 265 postgraduate and super speciality students and 158 undergraduate students. In recognition of their academic excellence, 46 meritorious students, comprising 29 postgraduate/super speciality and 17 undergraduate students, were awarded medals.

VMMC & Safdarjung Hospital Marks 25 Years

Established in 2001, Vardhman Mahavir Medical College and Safdarjung Hospital has completed 25 years of contribution to medical education, healthcare delivery and research. Over the years, the institution has played an important role in medical education and the development of healthcare professionals, while strengthening its academic and clinical capabilities.

The 8th Convocation, held during the Silver Jubilee Year, celebrates the achievements of graduating students and marks an important milestone in the institution’s continued commitment to excellence in medical education, research and patient care.

The occasion brought together Senior Officials of the Ministry, faculty members, graduating students and distinguished guests to celebrate the academic achievements of the graduating batch and commemorate the institution's 25 years of service in the field of medical education and healthcare.

Dr Loveneesh G. Krishna, Director General Health Services (DGHS), Ministry of Health and Family Welfare; Dr. Kavita Rani Sharma, Director, VMMC and Safdarjung Hospital, Dr. Geetika Khanna, Principal, VMMC and Safdarjung Hospital were also present at the event.

******

SR

Prime Minister's Office
PM to participate in the Valedictory Session of Departmental Summit on Social Justice and Empowerment on 19 November
Summit to deliberate on four key themes: Nasha Mukt Bharat, One Nation One Scholarship Portal, Early Intervention and Reduction of Disability Burden, Sugamya Bharat for Viksit Bharat
Posted On: 18 NOV 2026 7:53PM by PIB Delhi

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi will participate in the valedictory session of the Departmental Summit on Social Justice and Empowerment on 19 November 2026 at around 4:30 PM at Sushma Swaraj Bhawan, New Delhi. He will also address the gathering on the occasion.

The two-day Departmental Summit, being held on 18-19 November 2026, will bring together political leadership and officials from States dealing with the sectors of Social Justice and Empowerment and Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities. It is the third in the series of Departmental Summits envisioned by the Prime Minister to strengthen cooperative federalism, foster collective ownership of national priorities and accelerate outcomes through closer Centre-State collaboration.

The Summit will deliberate on four key thematic areas :

  1. Reimagining Prevention and Drug demand Reduction Strategy for a Nasha Mukt Bharat.
  2. One Nation One Scholarship portal- Accessible Scholarships, Empowered Students.
  3. Early Intervention and Reduction of Disability Burden
  4. Sugamya Bharat for Viksit Bharat.

The Departmental Summit provides a platform for the Union and State Governments to exchange experiences, share best practices and deliberate on key sectoral priorities, with a focus on addressing implementation challenges and improving governance and service delivery.

***

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
Union Health Secretary Smt. Punya Salila Srivastava Holds Review Meeting with Executive Directors of New AIIMS to Assess Institutional Performance and Strengthen Healthcare Delivery
18 Functional AIIMS Have 14,860 Operational Beds and 404 Functional Operation Theatres, Strengthening Tertiary Healthcare Services Across the Country
97.41 Lakh OPD Registrations, 4.91 Lakh IPD Admissions, 3.18 Lakh Surgeries and 629 Organ Transplants Recorded in New AIIMS in FY 2026-27 So Far
New AIIMS Publish 3,593 Research Papers in FY 2026-27 So Far, Reflecting Progress in Institutional Research and Academic Output
Smt. Srivastava Calls for Identifying Institute-Specific Areas of Excellence, Strengthening Regional Referral Linkages and Ensuring a Supportive, Stress-Free and Safe Environment for Students and Residents
Posted On: 18 NOV 2026 7:52PM by PIB Delhi

Union Health Secretary Smt. Punya Salila Srivastava reviewed the functioning of all the New AIIMS under Pradhan Mantri Swasthya Suraksha Yojana (PMSSY) in a meeting here today with all the Executive Directors of these Institutes of National Importance (INIs). Under PMSSY, 22 AIIMS have been approved, out of which 18 are functional with teaching, learning & research, IPD/OPD facilities, emergency & trauma, diagnostic facilities, Specialty and Super- Specialty Departments, AMRIT pharmacy, Jan Aushadhi Kendras, etc. and 4 AIIMS are at different stages of construction/operationalization.

Smt. Srivastava expressed her appreciation on the work being done by all the Executive Directors (EDs) in the seamless operations of the New AIIMS and took cognizance of the action taken on the decisions taken by the Central Institute Body (CIB) in its meeting held on 8th April, 2025. She reviewed the progress of all new AIIMS and assessed the status of the tertiary healthcare services, surgeries, diagnostics, operational efficiency of medical equipment, faculty/non-faculty positions, capital fund utilization, public grievances, etc. During the meeting, it was informed that currently, 14,860 Beds and 404 Operation Theatres (OTs) are functional in the 18 AIIMS. Around 97.41 lakh OPD registrations and 4.91 lakh IPD admissions have been undertaken in FY 2026-27 so far.

New AIIMS are operating comprehensive organ transplant programmes including kidney, liver, heart, cornea and bone marrow and around 629 organ transplants have been performed in FY 2026-27 so far. Advanced Clinical services are being offered in AIIMS and around 3.18 lakh surgeries have been performed this year. High–end diagnostics facilities have been established in all AIIMS including PACS (Picture Archiving and Communication System) in several AIIMS. During the meeting, it was informed that the research output has also increased and so far 3,593 research papers have been published this year.

Looking at the performance of the AIIMS, Union Health Secretary directed that “each AIIMS should identify its own areas of excellence and prepare a roadmap and actionable points. All efforts should be made to streamline the referral linkages with local hospitals in order to strengthen tertiary care facilities in the region as a whole.” She emphasized the importance of proactive and continuous measures to ensure a supportive, stress-free and safe environment in the Institutes for the mental wellness of students and residents.

Smt. Srivastava directed that all EDs to take all necessary steps to fill vacant faculty positions and hold Standing Selection Committee (SSC) meetings at least 4 times a year. She also directed that the Institutes must ensure optimal utilization of resources, especially of high-end diagnostic and therapeutic equipment. Highlighting the importance of sustaining public trust in AIIMS, she advised the EDs to be sensitive towards grievances and improve the quality of redressal in each Institute.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
Strengthening India’s Community Seed Banks (CSBs): DIVERSIFARM-India Maps 652 CSBs and Releases New Capacity-Building Manual
Posted On: 18 NOV 2026 7:39PM by PIB Delhi

India has at least 1,000 community seed banks (CSBs), according to a survey conducted by DIVERSIFARM-India. The project’s digital atlas has already mapped 652 of these community-led institutions, providing an important foundation for understanding, strengthening and supporting India's diverse community seed banks.  The outputs were shared at the National Seminar for the Advancement of CSBs held over two days on 17th and 18th November, 2026 at NASC, New Delhi. They include a GIS-based atlas with profiles of CSBs, a policy brief on CSB typologies, a roadmap for CSBs in Odisha, and a new capacity-building manual.

Addressing the event, Ms. May-Elin Stener, Ambassador of the Royal Norwegian Embassy in New Delhi, said  that the Embassy welcomed the project’s extensive mapping and support for community seed banks across India. She added that this project is an important component of the partnership between India and Norway.

Dr Regine Andersen, Research Professor, Fridtjof Nansen Institute (FNI), Norway, also shared several outputs from the three-year collaboration between FNI and MSSRF as the core partners of DIVERSIFARM-India. He said that the digital platform brings together community seed banks working across India and creates awareness about their strengths and collective efforts.

Dr Rengalakshmi R, Executive Director, MSSRF said that CSBs are more than just storehouses. She added that they are a living institution for in-situ conservation that builds farmers' resilience.

DIVERSIFARM-India is a project led by Fridtjof Nansen Institute (FNI) and the M S Swaminathan Research Foundation (MSSRF) that aims to improve food, nutrition, and livelihoods for small farmers by strengthening seed systems through community seed banks.

Six typologies to guide policy, One roadmap to shape the future of CSBs in Odisha

The comprehensive study had identified six CSB typologies based on management structures.Identifying these institutional differences is crucial for targeted and effective policy support.

Another policy brief under the project charts a 10-point roadmap for CSBs in Odisha. It recommends a secretariat under the Department of Agriculture and Farmers’ Empowerment, to shape and sustain environments that enable CSBs in the state.

Manual offers practical guide to establishing and sustaining CSBs

A capacity-building manual was also developed based on in-depth case studies conducted in Odisha, the pilot state. Combining technical guidance, organizational approaches and policy relevance, it is a practical guide to establish, manage and sustain CSBs in India.

The manual was released by Dr Trilochan Mohapatra, Chairperson, Protection of Plant Varieties and Farmers’ Rights Authority (PPVFRA) at National Agricultural Science Complex, New Delhi. Noting the PPVFRA’s support for CSBs in his inaugural address, he said now that government support is growing, he is sure that the Community Seed Banks would flourish.

Legal and policy landscape

The DIVERSIFARM-India project also examined the legal and policy landscape in India to better understand the bottlenecks and opportunities for CSBs. The Protection of Plant Varieties and Farmers Right Act (PPVFRA) and The National Biodiversity Act were identified for their demonstrated potentialin strengthening CSBs.

Padma Shri Dr P. L. Gautam, Former Chairperson, PPVFRA and NBA said that to further benefit farmers, a need to establish a synergy between the two laws emerged in discussions.  He added biodiversity is a common heritage of humankind,  reflecting on the founding principle of the laws.

Dr Devendra Kumar Yadava, Director, ICAR-National Bureau of Plant Genetic Resources, and DDG (Crop Science), ICAR, highlighted that community gene banks and national gene banks can be strengthened collaboratively. Echoing his recommendation, Padma Shri Dr PL Gautam also underscored committed funding and capacity building as the need of the hour.

For the CSB manual, the digital atlas and the policy brief on CSB typologies, Pleas click https://communityseedbanks.in/

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Education
Secretary, DoSEL, chairs interactive session with UN Special Rapporteur on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities
Ministry of Education highlights India's initiatives towards the implementation of the CRPD and promotion of inclusive and equitable education
Posted On: 18 NOV 2026 7:28PM by PIB Delhi

Secretary, Department of School Education & Literacy (DoSEL), Union Ministry of Education, Shri T. K. Anil Kumar, chaired an interactive session with United Nations Special Rapporteur (UNSR), Ms. Heba Hagrass, on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities in New Delhi on November 17, 2026. The discussions provided an opportunity to share perspectives on the initiatives undertaken by the Government towards strengthening inclusive education and promoting equitable access to educational opportunities for children with special needs (CwSN).

The Department highlighted the initiatives taken towards the implementation of the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (CRPD) including key interventions under Samagra Shiksha to strengthen inclusive education through a holistic, life-cycle approach covering early identification, individualised support, accessibility, therapeutic interventions, skilling and provision of exam-related facilities by the Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE).

The Department also highlighted PRASHAST, the disability screening checklist designed for early identification of 21 disabilities among school-going children aged 3 to 18 years. The revamped PRASHAST 2.0 mobile application, integrated with UDISE+, simplified the screening process, reducing the time required for initial screening by teachers from three days to 15 minutes. As of October 2026, over 6 crore children had been screened and more than 7.26 lakh schools had been onboarded on the PRASHAST portal, alongside sensitisation of over 79 lakh teachers.

Representatives from the United Nations, senior officials from the Ministries of Education and External Affairs attended the Session.

Ms. Heba Hagrass also visited Government Co-ed Senior Secondary School, at R. K. Puram, to review inclusive education interventions undertaken under Samagra Shiksha. She took stock of resource rooms with facilities and support mechanisms catering to CwSN students. She also interacted with parents of CwSN students to understand their experiences and perspectives on the support provided in schools.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment’s Pavilion at 45th IITF 2026 Records Cumulative Sales of ₹ 29.56 Lakh; Growing Consumer Patronage Boosts Economic Opportunities for Artisans
Cumulative Sales Register Approximately 70% Increase Over Previous Day, Reflecting Growing Appreciation for Indigenous Craftsmanship
Over 130 Artisans from 19 States Showcase India’s Rich Handicraft, Handloom and Cultural Heritage
Posted On: 18 NOV 2026 7:14PM by PIB Delhi

Continuing to witness an encouraging response from visitors, the pavilion of the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment at the ongoing 45th India International Trade Fair (IITF) 2026 at Bharat Mandapam, in the National Capital here, has recorded cumulative sales of approximately ₹29.56 lakh as of November 17, 2026, reflecting growing consumer appreciation for indigenous products and traditional craftsmanship.

The cumulative sales have registered an impressive increase of approximately 70 per cent from ₹17.37 lakh recorded as of November 16, 2026, with additional sales of approximately ₹12.19 lakh in a single day. The cumulative sales have also increased more than fivefold from ₹5.50 lakh recorded up to November 15, 2026, indicating growing consumer patronage and expanding market opportunities for participating artisans and entrepreneurs.

The Ministry’s pavilion, located at Hall No. 5, Ground Floor, ITPO, has emerged as a vibrant platform for showcasing India’s diverse artistic traditions, indigenous skills and entrepreneurial talent, while facilitating direct interaction between traditional artisans and consumers.

A Senior Official in the Ministry said more than 130 artisans from 19 States are showcasing their products at the ongoing Trade Fair through the Ministry’s three Apex Corporations, namely the National Scheduled Castes Finance and Development Corporation (NSFDC), National Backward Classes Finance and Development Corporation (NBCFDC) and National Safai Karamcharis Finance and Development Corporation (NSKFDC).

The participation of the Ministry’s three Apex Corporations at IITF 2026 further underscores their role in strengthening market linkages, promoting entrepreneurship and advancing the socio-economic empowerment of disadvantaged and marginalised communities, the Official noted.

He said the pavilion offers a diverse range of traditional handlooms, intricately crafted handicrafts, handcrafted jewellery, textiles, footwear, handmade articles and other indigenous products, reflecting the distinct artistic traditions and rich cultural heritage of different regions of the country.

The Official said the steady rise in sales highlights the growing recognition of the skills, creativity and entrepreneurial potential of traditional artisans. National-level exhibitions such as IITF provide an enabling platform for artisans to enhance product visibility, expand their consumer base and strengthen their economic prospects.

Beyond facilitating direct sales, the Trade Fair provides participating artisans with opportunities to understand evolving consumer preferences, explore contemporary market trends, establish new business connections and identify avenues for long-term entrepreneurial growth, the Official said.

The Official said guided by the vision of Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi and the principle of ‘Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas’, the Ministry continues to promote greater economic participation and self-reliance among artisans and entrepreneurs belonging to Scheduled Castes, Backward Classes, Safai Mitras and De-Notified, Nomadic and Semi-Nomadic Tribes (DNTs).

The Official said an important highlight of the Ministry’s participation at IITF 2026 is the promotion of the TULIP (Traditional Artisans’ Upliftment Livelihood Programme) brand, which seeks to establish a distinct market identity for artisan-made products and enhance their recognition among domestic and international consumers.

The TULIP initiative was recently launched by Hon’ble Union Minister for Social Justice and Empowerment, Dr. Virendra Kumar, during the Shilp Samagam Mela at Dilli Haat in the National Capital, he said.

He said the initiative aims to integrate traditional craftsmanship with contemporary market requirements, encourage innovation and entrepreneurship, and facilitate sustainable income-generating opportunities for artisans.

Through the promotion of the TULIP brand and participation in prominent national-level exhibitions, the Ministry is working towards strengthening an inclusive entrepreneurial ecosystem that enables traditional artisans to translate their skills and indigenous knowledge into sustainable economic opportunities, the Official remarked.

The Official said the visitors to the Ministry’s pavilion have an opportunity to experience India’s diverse cultural and artistic heritage, interact directly with artisans and contribute to their economic empowerment by purchasing authentic, indigenous and handcrafted products.

The ongoing 45th India International Trade Fair 2026, inaugurated on November 13, 2026, offers a prominent platform for trade, commerce, entrepreneurship and cultural exchange, bringing together producers and consumers from diverse backgrounds.

With the encouraging sales performance and sustained consumer engagement at IITF 2026, the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment continues to reaffirm its commitment to preserving India’s traditional artistic heritage, promoting indigenous products, strengthening sustainable livelihoods and fostering inclusive socio-economic development in line with the vision of Viksit Bharat@2047.

item.content:encoded:
AYUSH
Union Ayush Minister Shri Prataprao Jadhav Meets H.E. Mr. Roger Baro, Minister and Special Adviser to the President of Burkina Faso
India Keen to Work Closely with Burkina Faso in Traditional Medicine: Shri Prataprao Jadhav
Institutional Collaboration Will Open New Avenues for Traditional Medicine Cooperation: Shri Jadhav
Posted On: 18 NOV 2026 7:02PM by PIB Delhi

The Union Minister of State (Independent Charge), Ministry of Ayush, Shri Prataprao Jadhav, met with the delegation of Burkina Faso led by H.E. Mr. Roger Baro, Minister and Special Adviser to the President of Burkina Faso, in New Delhi today. The Burkinabe delegation is visiting India from 17 to 25 November 2026. The visit focuses on traditional medicine and Ayush institutions.

During the meeting, Shri Prataprao Jadhav said that India attaches great importance to its bilateral relations with Burkina Faso and is keen to further strengthen the partnership. He noted that the two countries share a rich heritage of traditional medicines and indigenous healthcare practices, which provides a strong foundation for cooperation in this field.

Shri Jadhav said he had learnt that the President of Burkina Faso, H.E. Captain Ibrahim Traore, had expressed interest in India’s support for the conservation and sustainable development of Burkina Faso’s traditional medicinal plants. He added that India is keen to work closely with Burkina Faso in the field of traditional medicines and is ready to share its experience and expertise, including in herbal medicine standardisation, quality assurance, pharmacopoeial standards and the regulatory framework.

Shri Jadhav welcomed institutional partnerships between Ayush institutions in India and relevant traditional medicine institutions in Burkina Faso. He noted considerable potential for a flagship India-Burkina Faso Project on Conservation and Sustainable Development of Traditional Plants, in collaboration with India’s National Medicinal Plants Board and relevant institutions in Burkina Faso.

The Minister said India is also keen to support the promotion of Yoga and Ayush-based wellness programmes in Burkina Faso. He said the two sides could explore the possibility of signing a Memorandum of Understanding between the Ministry of Ayush and Burkina Faso’s Ministry of Health to promote an institutional framework. He also welcomed Burkina Faso’s participation in future WHO Global Summits on Traditional Medicine and in programmes at the WHO Global Traditional Medicine Centre in Jamnagar, Gujarat. As an immediate step, he suggested that both sides identify nodal officers to take the proposal forward and work out specific areas of cooperation.

Highlighting India's commitment to South-South Cooperation and its engagement through G20 and BRICS, the Minister said India offers full support to Burkina Faso in achieving its developmental goals, and that the developmental partnership is guided by the needs and priorities set by the Government of Burkina Faso. He said India is also contributing to capacity building through training and scholarship initiatives under programmes such as ITEC, ICCR and the PCFD course, from which more than 250 Burkinabe nationals have benefited in the last few years.

The Minister noted that the small but vibrant Indian community in Burkina Faso has been making a positive contribution to the country’s socio-economic development. He said that India would appreciate the continued support of the Government of Burkina Faso in ensuring the safety and security of the community. He added that India is committed to working closely with Burkina Faso to promote traditional medicine through cooperation, knowledge exchange and capacity building. Shri Jadhav wished the delegation a successful and productive visit and said he looks forward to taking bilateral cooperation further.

The delegation included Prof. Rakissida Alfred Ouedraogo, Special Ministerial Advisor for Higher Education and Health Issues; Dr. Mariam Sawadogo/Bagayan, Director of Traditional and Alternative Medicine at the Ministry of Health, serving as the mission’s rapporteur; Prof. Aminata Pagnimdebsom Nacoulma, Lecturer-Researcher specialising in Pharmacognosy at Joseph Ki-Zerbo University; and Dr. Hyacinthe Bonkoungou, Specialised Pharmacist and Director of the Center for Traditional Medicine and Integrated Care.

The Burkina Faso Embassy was represented by Mr. Some Désiré Boniface, Ambassador; Mr. Zingué-ouattara Didier Christian, Deputy Chief of Mission; and Mr. Ouoba Joël, interpreter. From the Ministry of External Affairs, the meeting was attended by Shri O. P. Meena, Ambassador of India to Burkina Faso, and Shri Kailash Bhatt, Under Secretary (Central & West Africa), MEA. Secretary, Ministry of Ayush, Vaidya Rajesh Kotecha and senior officials of the Ministry of Ayush were also present at the meeting.

The meeting reaffirmed the shared commitment of India and Burkina Faso to deepen cooperation in traditional medicine and strengthen collaboration between Ayush institutions and their Burkinabe counterparts.

item.content:encoded:
Vice President's Secretariat
Vice-President Graces Silver Jubilee Celebrations and 8th Annual Convocation of Vardhman Mahavir Medical College and Safdarjung Hospital in New Delhi
Vice-President Calls upon graduating doctors to uphold compassion, integrity and scientific temper; says a medical degree is a commitment to humanity
Viksit Bharat Must Also Be a Swasth Bharat: Vice-President Highlights India’s Healthcare Transformation
Technology Must Never Replace the Human Connection Between Doctor and Patient: Vice-President
Posted On: 18 NOV 2026 6:58PM by PIB Delhi

The Vice-President of India, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, today graced the Silver Jubilee Celebrations and 8th Annual Convocation of Vardhman Mahavir Medical College (VMMC) and Safdarjung Hospital as the Chief Guest at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi. He distributed medals to outstanding postgraduate and undergraduate students on the occasion.

Congratulating the VMMC and Safdarjung Hospital fraternity on completing 25 years of dedicated service to medical education, healthcare and society, the Vice-President said that twenty-five years represented trust earned, lives touched, knowledge created and service rendered. He described the occasion as a celebration of a legacy of learning, healing and nation-building.

Referring to the remarkable expansion of India’s healthcare and medical education sectors, the Vice-President said that under the visionary leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi and the dynamism of Union Minister for Health and Family Welfare Shri Jagat Prakash Nadda, the country has made tremendous progress.

The Vice-President said that this expansion reflects the growing reach of higher education and India’s commitment to strengthening its healthcare system. The focus is now increasingly on quality healthcare, medical education, research and innovation, he added.

Emphasising that a medical degree is fundamentally a commitment to humanity, he said that the true measure of a doctor lies in the lives improved and dignity preserved. He urged the young doctors to let empathy accompany their expertise, integrity guide their decisions and scientific temper strengthen their professional practice.

Technology, he stressed, must never replace the human connection between a doctor and a patient. He called upon the graduates to listen patiently, communicate honestly and treat every individual with dignity, irrespective of their financial circumstances or social background.

Referring to the vision of Viksit Bharat @ 2047 articulated by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, the Vice-President said that a healthy, educated and empowered population would form the foundation of India’s national progress. The Prime Minister has repeatedly emphasised that a Viksit Bharat must also be a Swasth Bharat, he said, adding that initiatives such as Ayushman Bharat reflect the country’s commitment to making quality healthcare accessible and affordable to all.

Urging the graduating doctors to keep Nation First – Rashtra Pratham – in all their thoughts and actions, he encouraged them to dedicate their knowledge to healing and their compassion to inspiring others. He also urged everyone to say ‘No to Drugs’.

Recalling that VMMC bears the name of Lord Mahavira, the Vice-President observed that the philosophy of ‘Live and Let Live’ resonates deeply with the noble mission of the medical profession. He urged the graduates to uphold Lord Mahavira’s ideals of compassion, humanity and selfless service.

On the occasion, the Vice-President joined the students in taking the “No to Drugs” pledge. He also released the Silver Jubilee commemorative Coffee Table Book.

Union Minister for Health and Family Welfare and Chemicals and Fertilizers Shri Jagat Prakash Nadda, Director General of Health Services Dr. L. G. Krishna, Director, VMMC and Safdarjung Hospital Dr. Kavita Rani Sharma and Principal Dr. Geetika Khanna were among those present.

***

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Micro,Small & Medium Enterprises
Union Minister of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME) Shri Jitan Ram Manjhi inaugurates MSME, KVIC, COIR and NSSH Pavilions at the 45th India International Trade Fair
The theme of the MSME Pavilion this year is “MSME-Vikas Bhi, Virasat Bhi”
Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises is a vital sector for generation of employment to India's large youth population- Union Minister Shri Jitan Ram Manjhi
Posted On: 18 NOV 2026 6:51PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME), Shri Jitan Ram Manjhi, inaugurated the Ministry of MSME, Khadi & Village Industries Commission (KVIC), COIR and National SC-ST Hub (NSSH) Pavilions in Hall No. 6 at the 45th India International Trade Fair (IITF) at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, today. The event was also graced by Sushri Shobha Karandlaje, Minister of State in the Ministry of MSME. The theme of Pavilion this year is “MSME-Vikas Bhi, Virasat Bhi”.

Shri Bharat Khera, Secretary, Ministry of MSME and Dr. Rajneesh, Additional Secretary & Development Commissioner accompanied the delegates. Senior officers from the Ministry of MSME, Office of the Development Commissioner (MSME), Khadi & Village Industries Commission (KVIC), National Small Industries Corporation (NSIC) and COIR Board were also present on the occasion.

Following the inauguration, Union Minister Shri Jitan Ram Manjhi and Minister of State Sushri Shobha Karandlaje visited stalls in the Pavilions and witnessed live demonstration of various traditional manufacturing processes, encouraging the participants and exhibitors.

While speaking to the media, the Union Minister Shri Jitan Ram Manjhi said Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises are vital to provide employment opportunities to India's large youth population. The Government under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi has focused on the growth of the MSME sector. It is one of the highest employment generating sectors. Registration of MSMEs has now crossed 10 crore, generating employment to 42 crore persons. Udyam Assist Portal is making registration easier for micro enterprises. MSME Pavilion at IITF is a step towards inspiring and encouraging today’s youth to take up entrepreneurship, he added.

Highlights of the Pavilions

MSME Pavilion

  • The MSME Pavilion features 437 stalls including 292 participating MSME units from across the country, 101 from KVIC, 34 from NSSH and 10 belonging to Coir sector.
  • More than 98% of the MSME participants are first-time exhibitors, providing new entrepreneurs an opportunity to showcase their capabilities.
  • 29 States and Union Territories are represented, showcasing India's diverse entrepreneurial ecosystem.
  • 57.87% of women entrepreneurs are participating, highlighting women's growing role in the MSME sector.
  • 27.73% of SC/ST entrepreneurs are showcasing their products and enterprises.
  • Entrepreneurs with disabilities (PwD) are participating, reflecting the spirit of inclusive entrepreneurship.
  • 15 stalls have been set-up by PM Vishwakarma beneficiaries, providing them with a platform to showcase India's traditional art and craftsmanship.
     

The MSME Pavilion at IITF 2026 showcases India's rich regional diversity, traditional crafts and evolving manufacturing capabilities through an extensive range of products like-

  • Textiles, handloom and handicrafts
  • Green and eco-friendly products
  • PM Vishwakarma-made products and traditional artisan crafts
  • Glass, ceramics and metal crafts
  • Leather goods and beauty products
  • Games, toys and innovative utility products
  • Distinctive regional products and other specialized offerings

Bringing together enterprises from 29 States/UTs, the Pavilion provides a common platform for MSMEs to connect with buyers, visitors and industry stakeholders, fostering product visibility, market access and business opportunities.

The participation of women entrepreneurs, SC/ST entrepreneurs, persons with disabilities and PM Vishwakarma beneficiaries reflects the commitment to inclusive growth and expanding organised marketing opportunities for all enterprises.

The MSME Pavilion not only promotes India's indigenous products and entrepreneurial capabilities but also celebrates the contribution of MSMEs and skilled artisans in strengthening the country's economic and cultural landscape. Technology-focused exhibits showcasing drones and Chandrayaan components developed with MSME participation were displayed by CTTC Bhubaneswar, MSME TC Rohtak, IDEMI Mumbai and IGTR Ahmedabad.  

Coir Board Pavilion

The Coir Board Pavilion brings together the two research institutes of the Coir Board, namely the Central Coir Research Institute (CCRI) and the Central Institute of Coir Technology (CICT), along with artisan groups, Coir Board showrooms and sales depots, registered consignors and small-scale manufacturers.

The Pavilion provides a dynamic platform to showcase research outcomes, technological advancements and innovative applications in the coir sector. Key attractions include soilless cultivation, coir geotextiles, vertical gardens, coir wood, innovative biodegradable products, coir net houses, coir pith composting, CocoLoawn (portable coir-based lawn) and a selfie point featuring a coir rope wall.

National SC-ST Hub (NSSH) Scheme

Under the National SC-ST Hub (NSSH) Scheme, 34 SC/ST Micro and Small Enterprises (MSEs) from seven States have been facilitated with dedicated stalls. The initiative provides participating MSEs with an opportunity to showcase a diverse range of products, including handicrafts, textiles, engineering products and footwear, while connecting with institutional and bulk buyers.

It also supports the achievement of the Central Government's 4% public procurement target from SC/ST-owned MSEs. Participation in such events offers significant strategic advantages to SC/ST entrepreneurs by enabling them to establish direct business contacts, enhance brand visibility, receive valuable customer feedback and explore new markets, thereby promoting inclusive entrepreneurship and sustainable business growth.

Khadi India Pavilion

The Khadi India Pavilion at IITF 2026 offers an immersive experience of India's rich heritage, traditional craftsmanship and indigenous production processes through 101 stalls showcasing products made by artisans from different regions of the country. A key attraction this year is a specially created studio for the “Khadi Ki Baat” podcast, where conversations will be held with guests, artisans and Khadi enthusiasts to promote awareness and engagement around Khadi.

The Khadi Theme Pavilion also features live demonstrations of traditional charkha, peti charkha, and electrically operated potter's wheel, oil extraction using the traditional kolhu (ghani), handloom weaving and the making of soap, honey products, leather shoes, incense sticks and dhoop.
