item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
President of India inaugurates Golden Jubilee celebrations of ICMR–National Institute of Malaria Research
India records nearly 80 per cent decline in malaria cases and deaths between 2015 and 2025: President
President calls for sustained vigilance, effective surveillance and community participation to achieve malaria elimination
Scientific research must reach every village and every community where it is needed: President Murmu
President highlights ICMR’s contribution to malaria research and indigenous vaccine development
Union Health Minister Shri J.P. Nadda calls for intensified efforts to achieve malaria elimination by 2030
Number of malaria high-burden districts falls from 155 to 33: Union Health Minister Shri Nadda
Union Health Minister underscores the role of research and innovation in making healthcare affordable and accessible
Secretary DHR and DG ICMR calls for strengthening research to address emerging challenges in malaria control
ICMR–NIMR marks five decades of scientific research and contribution to malaria control
Posted On: 17 NOV 2026 6:55PM by PIB Delhi

The President of India, Smt. Droupadi Murmu, today inaugurated the Golden Jubilee celebrations of the Indian Council of Medical Research–National Institute of Malaria Research (ICMR–NIMR). Congratulating the past and present scientists, researchers and healthcare workers associated with the institute, the President recalled that malaria had historically been one of India's most serious public health challenges, particularly affecting rural and tribal communities. Sharing her personal experiences of witnessing the impact of malaria in villages, she highlighted how the disease affected people's livelihoods, education and future. She emphasised the importance of public awareness about completing the prescribed course of medication to ensure effective treatment and prevent recurrence.

The President highlighted India's progress in malaria control, noting that malaria cases and deaths had declined by nearly 80 per cent between 2015 and 2025, while the number of high-burden districts had reduced from 155 to 33. She also noted that 160 districts reported zero indigenous malaria cases during 2022–2025. Appreciating India's exit from the World Health Organization's (WHO) High Burden to High Impact (HBHI) group in 2024, she acknowledged the collective efforts of scientists, healthcare workers and citizens. She recognised ICMR–NIMR's contribution over five decades to research on malaria parasites, mosquito vectors, vector control, insecticide resistance and community surveillance.

Emphasising the need for continued vigilance and effective interventions, the President called for strengthened malaria diagnosis, treatment and surveillance, mosquito control, development of new medicines and vaccines, and greater public awareness and community participation. She stressed that scientific research and its outcomes should reach villages and communities where they are most needed. Drawing attention to emerging challenges such as climate change, unplanned urbanisation and increasing insecticide resistance among mosquitoes, she highlighted the importance of preventing waterlogging, eliminating mosquito breeding sources and strengthening environmental management. She also expressed satisfaction over ICMR–NIMR's contribution to the indigenous malaria vaccine being developed in Bhubaneswar and expressed confidence that it would support India's malaria elimination efforts.

The President also highlighted ICMR's contributions to research against tuberculosis, leprosy, kala-azar and COVID-19, including the establishment of a nationwide testing network and its partnership in the development of India's first indigenous COVID-19 vaccine. Referring to dengue as an emerging public health challenge, she called for effective research and diagnostic interventions. She also appreciated the role of the National One Health Mission in strengthening India's capacity to identify and address health risks emerging at the human-animal-environment interface. Emphasising the importance of indigenous medical technologies and affordable, quality healthcare, she called for stronger collaboration among research institutions, technical and higher education institutions and industry to realise the vision of Viksit Bharat by 2047.

Addressing the gathering, Union Minister of Health and Family Welfare Shri Jagat Prakash Nadda congratulated ICMR–NIMR on completing 50 years of dedicated scientific service. Describing the institute's contribution as a significant service to humanity, he appreciated its commitment to research and malaria prevention. He said that India's progress in malaria control over the past decade was the result of a comprehensive approach involving research on mosquito behaviour and malaria parasites, community participation, effective prevention, early diagnosis and appropriate treatment. Highlighting the decline of nearly 80 per cent in malaria cases between 2015 and 2025–26 and the reduction in high-burden districts from 155 to 33, he noted that India, which accounts for approximately 16 per cent of the global population, contributes around 0.7 per cent of global malaria cases and 0.6 per cent of malaria deaths. He appreciated India's exit from the WHO's High Burden to High Impact initiative and expressed confidence in achieving malaria elimination by 2030. “We will eliminate malaria by 2030 by bringing about the necessary changes in our strategies and policies,” he said, calling upon ICMR–NIMR to work with renewed commitment.

The Minister also appreciated ICMR's contributions to medical innovation, including MedTech Mitra, Patent Mitra and ELISA-based molecular diagnostics for dengue, chikungunya, Japanese encephalitis and other infectious diseases. Highlighting the Government's efforts to strengthen healthcare under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, he referred to the decline in out-of-pocket expenditure from 63 per cent to 42 per cent and the increase in government health expenditure from 6 per cent to 23 per cent. He called upon the scientific and healthcare community to intensify its efforts and contribute towards making India a leader in healthcare.

Secretary, Department of Health Research (DHR) and Director General, ICMR, Dr. Rajiv Bahl, highlighted ICMR–NIMR's 50-year journey since its establishment in 1977. He noted that the institute had evolved into one of India's premier institutions for malaria and vector-borne disease research, contributing to research on malaria vectors, parasite biology, insecticide resistance, treatment and diagnostics. He highlighted the Comprehensive Case Management Project in Odisha, undertaken in collaboration with the State Government, which demonstrated how universal access to testing, complete treatment and strengthened surveillance could substantially reduce malaria transmission, including in remote communities. He underlined the goals of zero indigenous malaria cases by 2027 and malaria elimination by 2030, and emphasised the need for stronger surveillance, interdisciplinary research and partnerships to address emerging challenges such as climate change, changing vectors and drug resistance. He reiterated ICMR's commitment to supporting research from basic scientific discovery and early-stage development to clinical evaluation of health technologies and interventions.

On this occasion, the President of India also released a commemorative postage stamp sheet marking the Golden Jubilee of ICMR–National Institute of Malaria Research, following its introduction by Ms. Mariamma Thomas, Member Postal Services Board.

The Union Minister of Health and Family Welfare released the ICMR–NIMR Coffee Table Book and the book ICMR–NIMR Research Journey: Five Decades of Science, Service and Impact. The first copies of the two books were presented to the President of India.

On the occasion, Director of ICMR-NIMR Dr Anup Anvikar highlighted the journey of NIMR in last 50 years through a video film depicting the Institute’s contribution in Malaria elimination efforts.

The Golden Jubilee celebrations mark five decades of ICMR–NIMR's contribution to malaria research and public health in India.

item.dc:creator: Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
item.description: Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment Stage Set for ‘Samaveshi Niti Sankalp’: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment Ready to Welcome Delegates from States, Union Territories for Two-Day Departmental Summit Extensive Preparations Completed for November 18–19 Summit in National Capital Focus on Strengthening Centre-State Partnership for Inclusive Socio Economic Development Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi to Grace the Valedictory Session More Than 13,500 Responses from Over 450 Districts to Shape Policy Deliberations and Strengthen Ground-Level Implementation Posted On: …
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
Stage Set for ‘Samaveshi Niti Sankalp’: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment Ready to Welcome Delegates from States, Union Territories for Two-Day Departmental Summit
Extensive Preparations Completed for November 18–19 Summit in National Capital
Focus on Strengthening Centre-State Partnership for Inclusive Socio Economic Development
Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi to Grace the Valedictory Session
More Than 13,500 Responses from Over 450 Districts to Shape Policy Deliberations and Strengthen Ground-Level Implementation
Posted On: 17 NOV 2026 6:06PM by PIB Delhi

With preparations in place and the stage set for a significant national-level dialogue on social justice and inclusive development, the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment is all set to welcome delegates, senior officials and representatives from States and Union Territories for the two-day Departmental Summit titled ‘Samaveshi Niti Sankalp’, scheduled to begin tomorrow, at Sushma Swaraj Bhawan, in the National Capital here.

The Ministry has completed the necessary preparations for the Summit, which will bring together representatives of the Union, State & UT Governments on a common platform to deliberate on key policy priorities, strengthen institutional coordination and work towards more effective implementation of welfare programmes.

The Summit will focus on advancing the vision of Viksit Bharat@2047 through a stronger Centre-State Partnership and a shared commitment to inclusive development.

The Hon’ble Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Modi, is scheduled to grace the Valedictory Session of the Summit, where the key outcomes and time-bound action plans emerging from the deliberations will be presented.

Secretary, Ministry of Social Justice And Empowerment, Shri Sudhansh Pant said the Departmental Summit is the third in a series of such summits envisioned by the Hon’ble Prime Minister to encourage collective ownership of national priorities, facilitate exchange of experiences and accelerate development outcomes through coordinated efforts between the Centre and the States.

He said in the run-up to the Summit, the Ministry has undertaken extensive consultations with State and Union Territory administrations, field-level functionaries and other stakeholders to ensure that policy discussions are informed by practical experiences and implementation-related insights.

The Secretary said a series of video conferences were held with State and Union Territory officials, while feedback was sought on four identified thematic areas from stakeholders within and outside the Government.

The consultation exercise received an encouraging response, with more than 13,500 responses from over 450 districts across the country, Shri Pant said. These valuable inputs have been incorporated into the background notes prepared for the Summit to facilitate informed, focused and outcome-oriented deliberations, he said.

Shri Sudhansh Pant said the Departmental Summit provides an important institutional platform for the Centre and States to come together, share successful practices, identify implementation challenges and explore innovative approaches for strengthening the delivery of welfare initiatives.

He said that the objective is to translate discussions into actionable strategies, with clearly defined timelines and shared responsibilities, ensuring that the benefits of government programmes reach their intended beneficiaries effectively.

The two-day Summit will deliberate on four key thematic areas namely ‘Reimagining Prevention and Drug Demand Reduction Strategy for a Nasha Mukt Bharat’; ‘One Nation, One Scholarship Portal – Accessible Scholarships’; ‘Empowered Students, Early Intervention and Reduction of Disability Burden’ and ‘Sugamya Bharat for Viksit Bharat’, Shri Pant further said.

The Secretary said these themes reflect the Ministry's continued focus on strengthening social inclusion, expanding access to welfare initiatives, improving institutional mechanisms and promoting the empowerment of aspirational sections of society.

The Secretary said the deliberations will be organised through four breakout sessions and two full-house sessions, providing opportunities for comprehensive discussions on the identified themes. He said all States and Union Territories will have dedicated opportunities and slots to make presentations during the breakout sessions and share their perspectives and comments in the full-house discussions.

Two experts will also share insights on international best practices to enrich the deliberations and encourage innovative approaches to programme implementation, he said.

Shri Pant said an important highlight of the Summit will be a Digital Exhibition showcasing the Ministry's key initiatives, flagship programmes and technology-driven interventions.

He said the Delegates will have the opportunity to explore integrated digital platforms such as ‘Samavesh’ and ‘e-Anudan’, Mobile Applications developed for field-level operations, and success stories demonstrating the impact of various schemes and programmes.

The exhibition will highlight how digital platforms, technological interventions and field-level innovations are contributing to improved service delivery, stronger institutional mechanisms and more effective implementation of welfare initiatives, the Secretary said.

The Secretary said the Ministry expects the Summit to facilitate the participating States for a meaningful exchange of ideas and formulation of actionable strategies and encourage mutual learning among States and Union Territories, towards achieving the vision of an inclusive, equitable and empowered society.

He said the key outcomes and action plans, along with defined timelines for implementation, will be presented before the Hon’ble Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Modi, during the Valedictory Session.

The Hon’ble PM’s guidance is expected to provide renewed impetus to the collective resolve of the Centre and States and strengthen decisive, coordinated and time bound action towards achieving the agreed outcomes and advancing the vision of Viksit Bharat@2047, the Secretary said.

With the preparations complete, the Ministry looks forward to welcoming representatives from across the country for two days of constructive dialogue, shared learning and collective commitment towards a more inclusive and empowered India, Shri Pant concluded.

item.title: ICAR and RIS Sign MoU to Strengthen Agricultural Cooperation and Knowledge Exchange Across the Global South
item.dc:creator: Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
item.description: Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare ICAR and RIS Sign MoU to Strengthen Agricultural Cooperation and Knowledge Exchange Across the Global South Partnership through DAKSHIN to promote sharing of agricultural technologies, best practices, capacity-building and mutual learning Posted On: 17 NOV 2026 5:31PM by PIB Delhi The Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) and the Research and Information System for Developing Countries (RIS) signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) on 17 November 2026 at New Delhi to strengthen agricultural…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
ICAR and RIS Sign MoU to Strengthen Agricultural Cooperation and Knowledge Exchange Across the Global South
Partnership through DAKSHIN to promote sharing of agricultural technologies, best practices, capacity-building and mutual learning
Posted On: 17 NOV 2026 5:31PM by PIB Delhi

The Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) and the Research and Information System for Developing Countries (RIS) signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) on 17 November 2026 at New Delhi to strengthen agricultural cooperation and knowledge exchange across countries of the Global South. The MoU was exchanged by Dr M. L. Jat, Secretary, Department of Agricultural Research and Education (DARE) and Director General, ICAR, and Prof. Sachin Kumar Sharma, Director General, RIS. The partnership, facilitated through DAKSHIN – Global South Centre of Excellence, will focus on sharing agricultural technologies, documenting best practices, knowledge exchange and capacity-building.

Speaking at the inaugural session of the High-Level Policy Dialogue on “Global South: Towards a New Strategic Partnership”, Shri Kirti Vardhan Singh, Minister of State for External Affairs, Government of India, emphasised that the Global South must strengthen its collective voice in shaping global narratives, building economic resilience and ensuring equitable access to emerging technologies, particularly Artificial Intelligence. He called for stronger India–Africa partnerships, greater institutional collaboration and active engagement of young researchers and policymakers in translating knowledge into meaningful policy outcomes.

Recalling the vision of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi at the Second Voice of the Global South Summit in November 2023, the Minister highlighted the importance of developing common perspectives on shared challenges, strengthening economic resilience and promoting affordable, scalable and locally relevant development solutions. He emphasised the need to move beyond traditional development cooperation towards co-development and shared solutions.

Dr M. L. Jat, Secretary, DARE and Director General, ICAR, highlighted ICAR's role as a century-old apex organisation for agricultural research, education and extension, with 114 research institutions, 152 regional research centres and 731 Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs), while coordinating with nearly 80 agricultural universities. He informed that ICAR has 74 Memoranda of Understanding with different countries and institutions, of which nearly 60 per cent are with institutions from the Global South.

Dr Jat emphasised that the partnership with RIS and DAKSHIN would further strengthen South–South collaboration by facilitating the exchange and application of available agricultural technologies, practices, systems, methods and tools across countries. He also highlighted the importance of identifying suitable agro-climatic and research domains to connect countries. He mentioned the proposed Science and Partnership Week in mid-April 2027, which will bring together participants from the Global South and North in India, and the idea of convening Global South and North leaders to discuss their respective needs and available capabilities through demand-driven partnerships.

Prof. Sachin Kumar Sharma, Director General, RIS, highlighted the importance of agriculture for the Global South and the need for knowledge sharing, mutual learning and cooperation. Drawing upon his experience in agricultural negotiations at the World Trade Organization (WTO), he highlighted the need to strengthen the voice and concerns of Global South countries in multilateral negotiations and global decision-making. He noted that RIS has a strong network across the Global South, while ICAR brings extensive agricultural technologies, research and best practices. He emphasised that the partnership would facilitate the sharing of Indian technologies and practices with other countries, particularly those with similar agro-climatic conditions, while also enabling mutual learning from partner countries.

H.E. Prof. Anil Sooklal, High Commissioner of South Africa to India, described the present global uncertainty as a defining moment for the Global South to assert its leadership in shaping a multipolar world order. He called for reforms in global governance, stronger strategic partnerships and the generation of knowledge and policy perspectives from within the Global South.

H.E. Mr Alem Tsehaye Woldemariam, Ambassador of the State of Eritrea to India and Dean of the Diplomatic Corps in India, emphasised the importance of translating the historical solidarity between India and Africa into meaningful partnerships through economic cooperation, connectivity, infrastructure development and youth engagement.

Ms Archna Vyas, Country Director, Gates Foundation, India, identified Digital Public Infrastructure, health security, agriculture and food systems, Artificial Intelligence and institutional capacity-building as promising areas for India–Africa cooperation. She stressed that effective partnerships must be grounded in country ownership, co-creation and mutual learning, with a focus on affordable and scalable solutions.

Dr Rajan Sudesh Ratna, Coordinator, DAKSHIN – Global South Centre of Excellence, reaffirmed DAKSHIN's commitment to moving from dialogue to actionable partnerships through country-led priorities, institutional cooperation and capacity-building.

 

The MoU signing took place during the two-day High-Level Policy Dialogue organised by RIS–DAKSHIN in partnership with the Ministry of External Affairs, Government of India, on 17–18 November 2026 at the India Habitat Centre, New Delhi, on the occasion of DAKSHIN Day 2026. The dialogue brings together diplomats, policymakers, researchers, development practitioners and representatives of academic and partner institutions to deliberate on strengthening South–South cooperation, with particular emphasis on the evolving India–Africa strategic partnership. The collaboration between ICAR and RIS aims to promote the exchange of agricultural technologies, knowledge, best practices and capacity-building opportunities across the Global South.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Science & Technology
Tribal communities have been the guardians of biodiversity: Dr Jitendra Singh
Dr Jitendra Singh addresses ‘Janjatiya Gaurav Divas’ programme organised by Ministry of Science & Technology
Tribal knowledge and STEM training can shape India’s scientific progress: Dr Jitendra Singh
Affordable, locally suited technologies can strengthen tribal economies, says the Union Minister
Technology compendium and booklet on STI for Tribal Empowerment released
Posted On: 17 NOV 2026 4:52PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science and Technology and Earth Sciences, and Minister of State in the Prime Minister’s Office, the Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions, the Department of Atomic Energy and the Department of Space, Dr Jitendra Singh, today called for tribal communities to be partners and leaders in India’s scientific and innovation journey.

Dr Jitendra Singh was addressing a programme marking Janjatiya Gaurav Divas, commemorating the birth anniversary of Bhagwan Birsa Munda. The programme was organised by the Department of Science and Technology’s (DST) SEED Division and the North East Centre for Technology Application and Reach (NECTAR). A technology compendium and a booklet on science, technology and innovation for tribal empowerment were released on the occasion.

Dr Jitendra Singh said Bhagwan Birsa Munda remains one of the greatest icons of India’s freedom struggle and a symbol of courage, self-respect and the aspirations of tribal communities. His life and contribution, the Minister said, continue to inspire efforts towards social justice, equality and inclusive development.

The Minister described tribal communities as guardians of biodiversity, living in harmony with forests, rivers and mountains. Dr Jitendra Singh said tribal knowledge and practices continue to inspire modern science, while digital education and STEM training can help tribal youth lead India’s scientific journey. The Minister called for technology-based enterprises, supported by skills, mentoring, finance and market linkages, to create livelihoods and strengthen local economies, particularly in the North Eastern Region.

The Minister said that the empowerment of tribal communities, particularly those living in remote and geographically challenging regions, is essential to achieving the vision of Viksit Bharat @2047.

The Union Minister emphasised the need for affordable, accessible technologies suited to local conditions and easy to operate and maintain. Citing sickle cell anaemia, Dr. Singh referred to a multi-institutional CRISPR-Cas9 gene therapy effort involving CSIR-IGIB, AIIMS New Delhi, CSIR-IICT Hyderabad, NII Mumbai and other institutions.

Dr Jitendra Singh said that Prof.Umesh V. Waghmare and the Department of Science and Technology had accomplished considerable work over the past few years to support Scheduled Tribe communities. He cited 124 new projects that benefited more than 75,000 people, particularly members of Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups, and 25 dedicated Science, Technology and Innovation (STI) Hubs across the country. Eleven Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe cells have also been set up in different States. Natural resource management programmes have benefited over 20,000 members of Scheduled Tribe communities.

The Union Minister said DST had also invited proposals to establish NIDHI Technology Business Incubator (TBI) hubs to promote startups with at least one founder from a Scheduled Tribe community. Dr Singh said there was immense talent waiting to emerge from these communities, which were not seeking charity but their due share of opportunities. He cited the INSPIRE-MANAK programme, in which 21,087 students from Scheduled Tribe communities in Classes 6 to 12 participated, forming a large share of the overall awardees.

Prof.Umesh V. Waghmare, Secretary, DST, said Janjatiya Gaurav Divas was an occasion to remember other tribal leaders who contributed to India’s freedom struggle and national development, and to acknowledge the contributions of tribal communities. He said working with tribal communities and including all sections of society are essential for the sustainable growth of the nation.

Prof. Ajay Sood, Principal Scientific Adviser to the Government of India, highlighted India’s strong research ecosystem and the potential to bring its technologies to communities at scale. Citing RuTAG and Rural Smart Village Centers, he said tribal communities, women and local entrepreneurs can lead technology-based enterprises that strengthen livelihoods and local economies.

The exhibition organised alongside the programme showcased innovative technologies and interventions developed through projects supported by DST and NECTAR for the benefit of tribal communities.

Dr Jitendra Singh congratulated DST and all the institutions and stakeholders associated with the programme, and reaffirmed the need to ensure that the benefits of India’s scientific and technological progress reach every corner of the country and every section of society.

Prime Minister's Office
Prime Minister meets with the President of the Republic of the Philippines on the sidelines of ASEAN Summit in Manila
Posted On: 17 NOV 2026 4:29PM by PIB Delhi

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi met H.E. Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr., President of the Republic of the Philippines, in Manila today on the sidelines of the ASEAN Summit.
Prime Minister congratulated the Philippines on its successful chairship of ASEAN this year. He appreciated the role of the Philippines as country coordinator for India in the ASEAN since 2024 and its continued support in strengthening ASEAN-India relations.
The leaders warmly recalled their recent meeting on the sidelines of the BRICS Summit in New Delhi in September 2026 where President Marcos Jr. was invited by PM Modi in the former’s capacity as ASEAN Chair. They appreciated the increased momentum in bilateral cooperation in various areas such as defence and security, space, railway infrastructure, fintech, and trade and investment under the aegis of the Strategic Partnership established between the two countries during the State Visit of President Marcos Jr. in August 2025. The leaders also exchanged views on key regional and global issues of mutual interest.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
India looks forward to Deepen Partnership with Small Island Developing States for Resilient Coasts and Oceans: Shri Bhupender Yadav at COP31 in Antalya (Türkiye)
Four Priority Areas for India–SIDS cooperation identified - Coastal Risk Assessment, Ecosystem Restoration, Renewable Energy and Capacity-building
Posted On: 17 NOV 2026 4:29PM by PIB Delhi

Antalya (Türkiye), 17th November, 2026

Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Shri Bhupender Yadav, today called for strengthening India's partnership with Small Island Developing States (SIDS) to build resilient coasts and oceans through knowledge-sharing, technology partnerships and practical cooperation. Addressing the high-level ministerial event on ‘India–SIDS Partnership for Resilient Coasts and Oceans: Sharing Knowledge, Technology and Solutions’ during UNFCCC COP31 in Antalya, Türkiye, the Minister emphasised that healthy oceans and resilient coastlines are fundamental to economic security, ecological stability and people's well-being. The event was organised by The Energy and Resources Institute (TERI) and the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Government of India, in partnership with the International Solar Alliance (ISA). It saw participation at ministerial level from the island nations of Mauritius (H.E. Mr. Rajesh Anand Bhagwan), Kiribati (H.E Mr. Tokaibure Rabaua), Marshal Islands (H.E. Mr. Jess Gasper), besides senior officials from the Government of Fiji (Mr. Andrew K. Coriakula), TERI and ISA.

Highlighting the growing challenges of sea-level rise, coastal erosion, ocean warming, coral bleaching, stronger storms and marine pollution, Shri Yadav said these are immediate concerns for island nations, affecting homes, infrastructure, livelihoods and, in some cases, the long-term habitability of their territories. Guided by the vision of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi and the principle of Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam, India believes that environmental protection and development must advance together, with climate resilience centred on people, livelihoods and ecosystems, he stated. Sharing India's experience in coastal resilience, the Minister highlighted the country's approximately 11,099-kilometre coastline and its efforts in scientific assessment, ecosystem conservation, shoreline management and disaster preparedness. He cited the Mangrove Initiative for Shoreline Habitats and Tangible Incomes (MISHTI), which advances mangrove conservation and restoration while supporting coastal livelihoods.

The Minister further highlighted India's experience in scientific coastal assessments, ocean forecasting and early warning systems, particularly in the States of Odisha and Andhra Pradesh, as important areas for knowledge exchange with SIDS. Through the International Solar Alliance (ISA), Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure (CDRI), Infrastructure for Resilient Island States (IRIS) and Forum for India-Pacific Islands Cooperation (FIPIC), India is seeking to deepen cooperation in renewable energy, disaster preparedness, resilient infrastructure and locally appropriate climate adaptation solutions, he informed.

Identifying four priority areas for enhanced India–SIDS cooperation, Shri Yadav called for collaboration on coastal risk assessment, shoreline monitoring and early warning systems; Ecosystem-based approaches covering mangrove conservation, coral reef and seagrass protection, wetland restoration and sustainable management of coastal and marine resources; Technology partnerships for Island context, focused on solar-powered solutions, decentralised renewable energy, water security and climate-resilient infrastructure; and Institutional partnerships and capacity-building to support joint project preparation and country-led pilot initiatives.

The Minister emphasised that cooperation must be guided by the priorities and national circumstances of individual countries, with solutions adapted to their geography, ecosystems and institutional capacities. He also underlined the importance of mutual learning, noting that SIDS, as custodians of extraordinary marine biodiversity and traditional knowledge, have valuable experience in adapting to changing ocean conditions. Shri Yadav expressed confidence that the dialogue would help identify concrete opportunities for collaboration and build partnerships extending beyond the meeting. Reaffirming India's readiness to share its experience and technical capabilities while learning from the priorities and knowledge of SIDS, he called for moving from shared challenges to shared solutions and from dialogue to action to protect oceans, strengthen coastal communities and secure a resilient future for generations to come.

Prime Minister's Office
Prime Minister addresses the 21st East Asia Summit in Manila
Posted On: 17 NOV 2026 4:13PM by PIB Delhi

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi addressed the 21st East Asia Summit (EAS) in Manila, today.

In the current era of crisis and conflicts, PM underscored the need for dialogue, mutual respect and cooperation to support all efforts for peace. Calling for a free, open, inclusive and rules-based Indo-Pacific, Prime Minister stressed that EAS must contribute towards bringing peace, stability and predictability in the global arena.

He particularly highlighted the impact of crisis and conflicts on food, fuel and fertilizer security the world over. He further called for ensuring safety and security of commercial ships and seafarers, who continue to be targeted in international waterways. Prime Minister underlined that India supports all efforts directed at peaceful resolution of the ongoing conflicts in Ukraine and West Asia.

He underscored the threats posed by terrorism to peace loving societies.

To strengthen cooperation across the EAS platform, Prime Minister proposed the following:

I) Seafarers’ Safety Initiative for cooperation in joint training and emergency response.

II) EAS Cyber Crime conference at National Forensic Science University to address new age threats from cross-border crimes such as online frauds and cybercrimes.

III) EAS Maritime Heritage Festival in Lothal.

IV) EAS University Conclave in Nalanda to foster greater academic cooperation with EAS countries.

Prime Minister congratulated the President of the Republic of the Philippines, H.E. Ferdinand R. Marcos for successfully organizing the Summit.

The full remarks of Prime Minister may be seen here [link].

item.content:encoded:
Prime Minister's Office
English Translation of Prime Minister’s Statement during the 21st East Asia Summit
Posted On: 17 NOV 2026 4:10PM by PIB Delhi

Your Excellency, President Marcos,
Your Majesty,
Excellencies,

Namaskar!

I warmly congratulate President Marcos for the excellent organisation of the East Asia Summit.

Friends,

Since the COVID pandemic, the world has been facing one crisis after another. Conflicts are putting increasing pressure on food, fuel, and fertiliser supplies.

Ships and seafarers are also being targeted on international waterways. Alongside the serious threat of terrorism, new forms of cross-border crime, such as cyber fraud and online scams, are also on the rise.

Friends,

Today, what the world needs most is peace, stability, and predictability.

For many years, the East Asia Summit has served as an important platform for finding solutions to shared challenges and strengthening mutual cooperation. This very spirit of dialogue, mutual respect, and cooperation is the cornerstone of India’s foreign policy.

ASEAN unity and centrality are at the heart of our Act East Policy. We are committed to a Free, Open, Inclusive, and Rules-based Indo-Pacific. Whether it is Ukraine or West Asia, we will continue to support every effort towards peace.

Friends,

Our seas are the lifelines of our shared prosperity. Ensuring their security and freedom of navigation is the responsibility of us all.

In this direction, we are launching a Seafarers' Safety Initiative, under which we will enhance cooperation in joint training and emergency response.

Friends,

Ensuring trust and security in the digital world is equally essential. At the AI Impact Summit held in India this year, we emphasized the development of human-centric, inclusive, and safe AI. We also emphasized the need for technologies such as digital watermarking to combat deepfakes and misinformation.

We welcome the Joint Statement issued today on combating online scams.

To effectively address this growing threat, we propose hosting the East Asia Summit Cyber Crime Conference at India’s National Forensic Sciences University.

Friends,

The foundation of our relationship lies in a shared heritage that goes back thousands of years. The National Maritime Heritage Complex, being developed at Lothal in India, will soon showcase this shared heritage to the world. To further strengthen our historical and cultural ties, we will also host the East Asia Summit Maritime Heritage Festival at Lothal.

Next year, we will host the East Asia Summit University Heads Conclave at Nalanda, which will provide fresh impetus to our cooperation in the fields of education and research.

Friends,

This year, we are commemorating the 50th anniversary of the historic Treaty of Amity and Cooperation in Southeast Asia.

Fifty years ago, this region gave the world an important message, the message of peace, respect for sovereignty, and dialogue. Today, that message has become even more relevant. Our shared future will be shaped not by conflict, but by mutual respect and cooperation.

With this vision, India will continue to stand shoulder to shoulder with ASEAN, remaining committed to regional peace, stability, and shared prosperity.

Thank you very much.

DISCLAIMER -This is the approximate translation of Prime Minister's remarks. Original remarks were delivered in Hindi.

**********

MJPS/SS/VJ/ST

Prime Minister's Office
Prime Minister meets with the Prime Minister of the Kingdom of Thailand on the sidelines the ASEAN Summit in Manila
Posted On: 17 NOV 2026 4:02PM by PIB Delhi

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi met with H.E. Mr. Anutin Charnvirakul, Prime Minister of the Kingdom of Thailand, on the sidelines of the 23rd India - ASEAN Summit and 21st East Asia Summit in Manila on 17 November 2026.

The meeting provided an opportunity to review the progress made in bilateral ties, which were elevated to Strategic Partnership during Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi's visit to Thailand in April 2025. The two leaders discussed ways to further deepen cooperation across key sectors, including trade and investment, defence and security, connectivity, digital technologies and fintech, culture, tourism and people-to-people ties. They also underscored the importance of working closely together in regional forums such as BIMSTEC, IORA, Mekong Ganga Cooperation, and the ASEAN-led architecture. Both leaders also exchanged views on various regional and global issues of mutual importance and reaffirmed their commitment to further strengthening their partnership.

India and Thailand share a time-tested friendship rooted in their shared civilizational and cultural heritage, people-to-people ties and mutual trust. Thailand is an important partner within the framework of India's Act East Policy and our Comprehensive Strategic Partnership with ASEAN.

***

Prime Minister's Office
Prime Minister meets with the Prime Minister of Singapore on the sidelines of the ASEAN Summit in Manila
Posted On: 17 NOV 2026 4:00PM by PIB Delhi

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi met today H.E. Mr. Lawrence Wong, Prime Minister of Singapore, on the sidelines of the 23rd India - ASEAN Summit and 21st East Asia Summit in Manila.

The leaders reviewed progress under the Roadmap for the Comprehensive Strategic Partnership, adopted during Prime Minister Wong’s Official Visit to India in September 2025, and discussed the way forward across the eight priority areas including economic cooperation, skills development, digitalisation, sustainability, connectivity, healthcare and medicine, defence and security cooperation, and people-to-people and cultural exchanges. The leaders also exchanged views on regional and global developments.

Prime Minister conveyed his best wishes for Singapore's upcoming Chairship of ASEAN. He assured Prime Minister Wong of India's full support for its success.

***

MJPS/SS/VJ/SS

item.content:encoded:
AYUSH
9th Naturopathy Day to Be Observed Across India on 18 November
‘Prakritik Chikitsa, Swasth Bharat’ to be the Theme of This Year’s Observance
National Programme to Be Held at the Central Research Institute of Yoga and Naturopathy, Nagamangala, Karnataka
Focus on Preventive Healthcare, Obesity Prevention and Lifestyle-Related Disorders
Posted On: 17 NOV 2026 3:36PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Ayush will observe the 9th Naturopathy Day on 18 November 2026 at the Central Research Institute of Yoga and Naturopathy (CRIYN), Nagamangala, Karnataka, under the theme ‘Prakritik Chikitsa, Swasth Bharat’. The observance will highlight the role of naturopathy in promoting preventive healthcare, healthy lifestyles and overall well-being, with a special focus on addressing obesity and lifestyle-related disorders.

To mark the importance of the day, the inaugural session of the main event at Nagamangala will see many initiatives of importance and of wider reach. Among the key highlights will be a dedicated community health initiative alongside several other impactful programmes that will serve as the main attraction of the event, aiming to foster holistic well-being and sustainable community development. These programs are thoughtfully designed to engage participants from all walks of life and create lasting positive change across the region. Together, they underscore a strong commitment to public welfare and inclusive progress.

This year's theme underscores the importance of adopting healthier lifestyles through appropriate dietary practices, physical activity, yoga, stress management, and other evidence-informed naturopathic approaches contributing to a healthier India. It seeks to strengthen public awareness about the importance of prevention and encourage individuals and communities to take an active role in maintaining their health and well-being. The observance also aligns with the Prime Minister's vision for a Fit and Healthy India, emphasising preventive healthcare and healthy living.

As part of the nationwide outreach, the observance will feature ten sub-themes focusing on different sections of society and key areas of public health. These include ‘Mother Nature – Healthy Mother, Healthy Family’, ‘Swastha Mahila – Fit & Healthy Women’, ‘Fit Force – Strong, Lean & Healthy Force’, ‘Healthy Campus – Fit Students, Healthy Nation’, ‘Healthy Workplace – Fit Workforce’ and ‘Safe Journey – Fit Driver, Safe Journey’.

The other sub themes include ‘Golden Wellness – Active Ageing, Healthy Ageing’, ‘Prakriti se Samarth – Healthy & Active Living’, ‘Natural Strength for Sporting Excellence’ and ‘Prakriti Kisan – Fit Farmer, Healthy Nation’. These initiatives seek to extend the message of naturopathy to families, women, students, working professionals, armed forces personnel, senior citizens, sportspersons and farmers, encouraging healthier practices across communities.

The observance will also highlight the efforts of the Ministry of Ayush towards strengthening the institutional, research and healthcare infrastructure for yoga and naturopathy in the country. Through its research institutions and initiatives, the Ministry is working to advance scientific research, education and the wider integration of naturopathy in preventive and promotive healthcare.

The 9th Naturopathy Day will serve as a platform to strengthen public engagement with naturopathy and reinforce the importance of healthy lifestyles, preventive healthcare and community participation in building a Swasth Bharat.

***

item.content:encoded:
Lok Sabha Secretariat
WOMEN’S REPRESENTATION MUST EXTEND FROM PANCHAYATS TO PARLIAMENT; HOPEFUL OF IMPLEMENTATION OF NARI SHAKTI VANDAN ADHINIYAM: LOK SABHA SPEAKER
WOMEN’S GREATER PARTICIPATION IN POLICYMAKING AND LEGISLATION WILL MAKE DEMOCRACY MORE RESPONSIVE AND ACCOUNTABLE: LOK SABHA SPEAKER
AI AND TECHNOLOGY CAN STRENGTHEN TRANSPARENCY, ACCOUNTABILITY AND EFFECTIVENESS OF DEMOCRATIC INSTITUTIONS: LOK SABHA SPEAKER
INSTITUTIONAL FRAMEWORK TO BE DEVELOPED FOR DIGITAL EMPOWERMENT AND CAPACITY-BUILDING OF WOMEN REPRESENTATIVES: LOK SABHA SPEAKER
LOK SABHA SPEAKER INAUGURATES THE FIRST COMMONWEALTH WOMEN PARLIAMENTARIANS (CWP) INDIA REGION CONFERENCE IN BENGALURU; CM, KARNATAKA AND OTHER DIGNITARIES GRACE THE OCCASION
Posted On: 17 NOV 2026 3:32PM by PIB Delhi

Lok Sabha Speaker Shri Om Birla today emphasized the need for greater representation of women across all democratic institutions. Shri Birla noted that women must have an effective role not merely as participants but also in leadership, policymaking and law-making. Referring to the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam enacted in 2023, he expressed hope that the provision for 33 per cent representation of women in the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies would move towards implementation, enabling women's leadership to extend from Panchayats to Parliament. He noted that several States have already provided for 50 per cent representation of women in Panchayats and Municipalities. Greater participation of women in legislative institutions and decision-making processes would contribute to building a stronger, more sensitive and accountable democracy. Women bring sensitivity, commitment and a strong sense of responsibility to public life, qualities that are particularly important in addressing the aspirations and challenges of society. Highlighting the pivotal role of women in strengthening democratic institutions, Shri Birla mentioned that greater participation of women in policymaking, legislation and decision-making would make democracy more responsive, inclusive and accountable. Shri Birla made these observations while inaugurating the First Commonwealth Women Parliamentarians (CWP) India Region Conference at Bengaluru.

Noting that Artificial Intelligence (AI) and technology are transforming every sphere of social life and, when used responsibly and accountably, he observed that AI can bring significant improvements in governance. He emphasised that public representatives must leverage technology and e-governance to strengthen their engagement with citizens, understand their problems and ensure timely and effective solutions. Technology can play a vital role in establishing transparent, accountable and efficient systems of governance. Observing that Parliamentary Committees function as ‘Mini Parliaments’, the Speaker said that these committees have made valuable contributions towards addressing the socio-economic challenges faced by women and have made important recommendations to the Government. AI and technology can further strengthen their monitoring and oversight functions and make their work more effective. He indicated that a dedicated session on AI and technology would be organised to enhance the understanding and capacities of women Members of Parliament and legislators in this regard.

The Speaker called for the need to develop an institutional framework to strengthen the capacities of elected women representatives across Panchayats, Municipalities, State Legislative Assemblies and Parliament. The initiative should focus on enabling women representatives, including Panchayat Sarpanches and Municipal Chairpersons, to effectively use AI, technology and digital platforms for public engagement, monitoring and ensuring transparency in governance, he noted. Shri Birla stressed that the ability of public representatives to use technology effectively would directly influence the quality of outcomes delivered to citizens, particularly women and people at the grassroots level. He also underscored the importance of mentorship by experienced women legislators to guide emerging leaders and strengthen their legislative and leadership capabilities.

Shri Birla opined that women have made significant contributions to India's journey from the freedom struggle to nation-building and are today providing leadership in virtually every sphere, including education, science, technology, research, entrepreneurship, sports, defence, space and politics. He said that technology and digital platforms are creating new opportunities for women's economic self-reliance and expanding their participation in social and political life. At the same time, empowering women digitally and ensuring a safe digital environment remain important priorities. Highlighting Karnataka's rich democratic heritage, the Speaker referred to the twelfth-century Anubhava Mantapa of Lord Basaveshwara as an important symbol of the region's democratic traditions. He also recalled the courage and valour of Kittur Rani Chennamma, whose legacy continues to inspire generations.

Shri Birla hoped that the two-day conference would provide an important platform for women parliamentarians and legislators from Commonwealth countries to exchange experiences, innovations and best practices. He observed that dialogue, discussion and the exchange of diverse perspectives, including agreement and disagreement, constitute the strength of democracy. Sharing successful practices from different legislatures would help strengthen democratic institutions and promote innovation from Panchayats to Parliament. Expressing confidence in the outcomes of the conference, the Speaker said that women's leadership would help take the nation towards a more inclusive, balanced and just society, with democratic institutions becoming stronger, more accountable and result-oriented, ensuring that the voice of the last person in society is heard and addressed.

Earlier, the Speaker welcomed the participants and thanked Dr. D. Purandeswari, Chairperson of the Commonwealth Women Parliamentarians Conference in India, the Chief Minister of Karnataka and the Presiding Officers of the Karnataka Legislative Assembly and Legislative Council for their initiative and efforts in organising the conference.

AS INDIA MOVES TOWARDS THE VISION OF VIKSIT BHARAT BY 2047, THE ROLE OF WOMEN IN SHAPING THE NATION'S FUTURE: SMT. D. PURANDESWARI

Addressing the gathering, Chairperson, CWP India Region, Dr. Daggubati Purandeswari noted that women's empowerment in a democracy cannot be measured only by the number of women occupying public offices. It must also be reflected in their ability to participate meaningfully in legislative debates, influence policy decisions, exercise leadership and contribute to the governance and development of the nation. She stressed that we must move beyond ensuring representation towards creating an enabling environment in which women can exercise their leadership with much aplomb and effectiveness. Appreciating Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam, 2023, she said that the legislation represents a historic step towards strengthening women's political representation. Greater participation of women in legislatures will bring wider perspectives, experiences and concerns into public policy and democratic deliberations, she added.

Speaking on the Theme of the Conference, the Chairperson of the CWP India Region observed that the outcome of the discussions in the Conference should not remain confined to resolutions and recommendations. We must strive to develop an actionable framework for strengthening gender-sensitive parliamentary institutions and enhancing the leadership capabilities of women public representatives, she suggested. She further noted that as India moves towards the vision of Viksit Bharat by 2047, the role of women in shaping the nation's future will be decisive and a developed India cannot be realised without the equal participation, leadership and contribution of its women.

Chief Minister, Karnataka, Shri D. K. Shivakumar delivered the Keynote Address. Deputy Chairman, Rajya Sabha, Shri Harivansh; Deputy Chief Minister, Karnataka, Dr. G. Parameshwara; and Speaker, Speaker, Karnataka Legislative Assembly, Shri G. S. Patil also addressed the gathering on this occasion. Chairman, Karnataka Legislative Council, Shri Saleem Ahmed delivered the Welcome Address and Deputy Chairman, Karnataka legislative Council, Dr. Umashree delivered the Vote of Thanks.

135 women law makers from Parliament of India and State Legislatures are participating in the two - day Conference. Theme of the Conference is ‘Strong Foundations, Stronger Voices: Inclusive Cyberspace and Mentorship Pathways for New Women Legislators’. Two Plenary Sessions will be held during the Conference: (i) ‘Empowering Women Digitally: Safe Cyberspace, Smart Choices’, and (ii)  ‘Capacity Building and Mentorship for Women Legislators’, In a special initiative complementing the broader deliberations, UN Women India will organise a side event on Menopause on 17 November 2026. The Conference will conclude on 18 November 2026 with the Valedictory Address of Governor, Karnataka, Dr. Sudha Yadav.

The Conference is expected to achieve the following outcomes:

  1. Facilitate the exchange of experiences, perspectives and good practices on creating safe and inclusive cyber space and digital empowerment for women legislators.
  2. Identify effective frameworks to mentorship, capacity building and leadership development, particularly for newly elected women legislators.
  3. Explore the ways to strengthen institutional safeguards and mechanisms to ensure meaningful participation of women in parliamentary processes.
  4. Promote cooperation and collaboration among legislatures in advancing women's parliamentary leadership.

 

बेंगलुरु के विधान सौध में आयोजित First Commonwealth Women Parliamentarians Conference के उद्घाटन सत्र को संबोधित किया। इस अवसर पर Commonwealth Countries की महिला सांसदों एवं विभिन्न राज्यों एवं केंद्र शासित प्रदेशों से आए विधायकों और जनप्रतिनिधियों के साथ महिला नेतृत्व और लोकतांत्रिक संस्थाओं में उनकी प्रभावी भागीदारी पर विचार साझा किए। भगवान बसवेश्वर के ‘अनुभव मंडपम’ की गौरवशाली लोकतांत्रिक परंपरा और कित्तूर की रानी चेन्नम्मा के अदम्य शौर्य की साक्षी कर्नाटक की यह धरती ज्ञान, नवाचार और प्रगतिशील चेतना की विशिष्ट पहचान रखती है। भारत के स्वतंत्रता संग्राम, संविधान निर्माण और राष्ट्र के नवनिर्माण में महिलाओं का योगदान अविस्मरणीय रहा है। आज वे शिक्षा, विज्ञान, प्रौद्योगिकी, खेल, अंतरिक्ष, रक्षा और राजनीति सहित प्रत्येक क्षेत्र में अपनी प्रतिभा एवं नेतृत्व से नए प्रतिमान स्थापित कर रही हैं। वर्तमान समय में AI और डिजिटल माध्यमों का उत्तरदायी एवं नैतिक उपयोग नीति निर्माण, विधायी कार्यवाही, जनसंवाद और सुशासन को अधिक प्रभावी बना सकता है। ऐसे में, technology और AI के इस युग में महिलाओं का Digital Empowerment तथा उनके लिए सुरक्षित Cyber Space सुनिश्चित करना हमारी सामूहिक जिम्मेदारी है। महिला सांसद केवल जनप्रतिनिधि ही नहीं हैं बल्कि स्वयं में institution हैं। अनुभवी महिला जनप्रतिनिधियों की Mentorship, निरंतर संवाद और Capacity Building के माध्यम से नई पीढ़ी के नेतृत्व को दिशा एवं सामर्थ्य प्रदान किया जाना चाहिए। मेरा दृढ़ विश्वास है कि जब महिलाओं को पंचायत से पार्लियामेंट तक समान अवसर, सुरक्षित वातावरण और निर्णय प्रक्रिया में प्रभावी भागीदारी मिलेगी, तब लोकतंत्र की जड़ें और अधिक गहरी होंगी। महिला नेतृत्व की शक्ति, संवेदनशीलता और उत्तरदायित्व से भारत का लोकतंत्र अधिक समावेशी, पारदर्शी, जवाबदेह और सशक्त बनेगा। यही सामर्थ्य विकसित भारत 2047 की संकल्पना को साकार करने का आधार बनेगा। #CWPIndia #WomenInParliament

— Om Birla (@ombirlakota) November 17, 2026

First Commonwealth Women Parliamentarians (CWP) India Region Conference में सहभागिता के लिए Karnataka विधानमंडल भवन (Vidhana Soudha), Bengaluru पहुँचने पर राज्य के माननीय मुख्यमंत्री श्री D.K. Shivakumar, कर्नाटक विधान परिषद के माननीय सभापति श्री Saleem Ahmed, माननीय विधान सभा अध्यक्ष श्री G.S. Patil, CWP India Region की सभापति डॉ. D. Purandeswari एवं अन्य गणमान्यों द्वारा किए गए आत्मीय स्वागत से अभिभूत हूँ। #CWPIndia #WomenInParliament

— Om Birla (@ombirlakota) November 17, 2026

आज बेंगलुरु के विधान सौध में आयोजित प्रथम First Commonwealth Women Parliamentarians India Region Conference के उद्घाटन सत्र में सम्मिलित होकर संबोधित करूँगा। इस अवसर पर सम्मेलन में सम्मिलित हो रहे महिला सांसदों एवं विभिन्न राज्यों एवं केंद्र शासित प्रदेशों से आए विधायकों और जनप्रतिनिधियों के साथ संवाद करूँगा। महिला नेतृत्व, विधायी संस्थाओं में उनकी प्रभावी भागीदारी, डिजिटल सशक्तीकरण एवं सुरक्षित साइबरस्पेस तथा महिला जनप्रतिनिधियों के क्षमता निर्माण और मेंटरशिप को समर्पित यह सम्मेलन अनुभवों के आदान-प्रदान और सार्थक विमर्श का महत्वपूर्ण मंच है। विश्वास है कि यह पहल महिला नेतृत्व को नई दिशा देने के साथ लोकतांत्रिक संस्थाओं को अधिक समावेशी एवं सशक्त बनाने और विकसित भारत 2047 के संकल्प को गति प्रदान करेगी। Live Link: https://t.co/63VtHEAu00

item.title: India’s Electronic Goods Exports Grow 44% to USD 31.97 Billion in April–September FY 2026-27
item.dc:creator: Ministry of Commerce & Industry
item.description: Ministry of Commerce & Industry India’s Electronic Goods Exports Grow 44% to USD 31.97 Billion in April–September FY 2026-27 Smartphone Exports Grow 35.8% to USD 18.17 Billion Non-Smartphone Electronics Exports Rise 56.5% to USD 13.79 Billion in April–September FY 2026-27 Posted On: 17 NOV 2026 3:26PM by PIB Delhi India’s electronic goods exports registered strong growth of 44.0% during April–September FY 2026-27, increasing from USD 22.20 billion in the corresponding period of FY 2025-26 to USD 31.97 billion. While smartphones continued to account…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Commerce & Industry
India’s Electronic Goods Exports Grow 44% to USD 31.97 Billion in April–September FY 2026-27
Smartphone Exports Grow 35.8% to USD 18.17 Billion
Non-Smartphone Electronics Exports Rise 56.5% to USD 13.79 Billion in April–September FY 2026-27
Posted On: 17 NOV 2026 3:26PM by PIB Delhi

India’s electronic goods exports registered strong growth of 44.0% during April–September FY 2026-27, increasing from USD 22.20 billion in the corresponding period of FY 2025-26 to USD 31.97 billion. While smartphones continued to account for the largest share of the electronics export basket, non-smartphone electronics recorded significantly faster growth, reflecting the broadening and diversification of India’s electronics exports across components, printed circuit boards, communication equipment, memory products and storage devices.

Exports of smartphones (HS 85171300) increased by 35.8%, from USD 13.38 billion in April–September FY 2025-26 to USD 18.17 billion during April–September FY 2026-27. Smartphones continued to be the largest component of India’s electronic goods exports. However, their share in total electronic goods exports moderated from 60.3% to 56.8%, amid faster growth in other electronics segments.

Non-smartphone electronics exports recorded a growth of 56.5%, increasing from USD 8.81 billion to USD 13.79 billion during the period. Consequently, the share of non-smartphone electronics in total electronic goods exports increased from 39.7% to 43.2%, indicating a broadening of India’s electronics export basket.

Exports of parts and accessories comprising mounted printed circuit boards (HS 84733030) increased from USD 63.3 million to USD 2.10 billion, registering growth of 3,219%. Singapore was the leading destination, with exports reaching USD 1.87 billion, followed by China at USD 111.5 million.

Exports of populated, loaded or stuffed printed circuit boards (HS 85177910) also registered significant growth of 304%, increasing from USD 213.7 million to USD 864.1 million. China was the leading destination at USD 789.2 million, while exports to Hong Kong increased from USD 5.9 million to USD 25.3 million.

Exports of network transmission and routing equipment (HS 85176290) nearly doubled, rising by 98% from USD 732.9 million to USD 1.45 billion. Hong Kong led the growth, with exports increasing from USD 264.7 million to USD 857.7 million. The United States and the Netherlands were also important destinations, with exports of USD 130.9 million and USD 124.4 million, respectively.

Exports of memory integrated circuits (HS 85423200) recorded growth of 2,333%, increasing from USD 23.1 million to USD 562.4 million. Malaysia emerged as the largest destination at USD 390.8 million, followed by Singapore at USD 102.4 million and Hong Kong at USD 25.2 million.

Similarly, exports of solid-state non-volatile storage devices (HS 85235100) increased by 1,680%, from USD 14.6 million to USD 260.5 million. China was the leading destination at USD 108.6 million, followed by Singapore at USD 76.8 million, Hong Kong at USD 22.3 million and the United States at USD 20.7 million.

The growth in India’s electronics exports reflects an increasingly diversified export basket, with non-smartphone electronics registering faster growth and gaining a larger share in overall exports. While smartphones continued to remain the largest component, with exports reaching USD 18.17 billion, the non-smartphone segment recorded stronger growth, increasing its contribution to total electronic goods exports.

The expansion across printed circuit boards, communication equipment, memory integrated circuits and solid-state storage devices, along with rising exports to markets such as Singapore, China, Hong Kong and Malaysia, underscores the growing contribution of these segments to India’s electronics export growth.

***

Abhishek Dayal/ Shabbir Azad/ Ishita Biswas

item.content:encoded:
President's Secretariat
PRESIDENT OF INDIA INAUGURATES THE YEAR-LONG GOLDEN JUBILEE CELEBRATIONS OF INDIAN COUNCIL OF MEDICAL RESEARCH-NATIONAL INSTITUTE OF MALARIA RESEARCH
PREMIER INSTITUTIONS LIKE THE ICMR CAN TAKE THE LEAD IN ACHIEVING THE HEALTH-RELATED GOALS OF VIKSIT BHARAT THROUGH RESEARCH, COLLABORATION AND INNOVATION: PRESIDENT DROUPADI MURMU
Posted On: 17 NOV 2026 2:58PM by PIB Delhi

The President of India, Smt Droupadi Murmu inaugurated the year-long Golden Jubilee Celebrations of the Indian Council of Medical Research-National Institute of Malaria Research in New Delhi today (November 17, 2026). 

Speaking on the occasion, the President said that malaria has long been a serious public health challenge in many countries around the world, including India. At the time of independence, it was one of the most critical public health challenges in our country. It is a matter of satisfaction that India has made remarkable progress in malaria control over the last few years. Improved healthcare services, modern diagnostic techniques, effective medicines, mosquito-control campaigns, and community participation have played a significant role in curbing the spread of this disease. India’s progress toward malaria elimination has received global recognition. In 2024, India moved out of the World Health Organization’s ‘High Burden to High Impact’ category. This achievement has been made possible through the collective efforts of our public health programs, scientists, healthcare workers, and citizens. The National Institute of Malaria Research has played a pivotal role in this long battle against malaria. Over the past five decades, it has conducted pioneering research in areas such as malaria parasites, mosquitoes, vector control, insecticide resistance, and community-based surveillance.

The President said that new challenges, such as climate change, unplanned urbanization, and the growing resistance of mosquitoes to insecticides, could pose fresh obstacles to the eradication of malaria. In such a scenario, the efforts of healthcare workers alone cannot prevent the spread of malaria. It is also necessary to focus on preventing water stagnation, eliminating mosquito breeding sources, and managing the environment. She expressed confidence that policymakers and the scientific community are making concerted efforts in this direction.

The President said that in recent years, dengue has also emerged as a major challenge in the country. This challenge is likely to become even more formidable due to global warming and shifts in monsoon patterns. Research and studies conducted by the ICMR have provided direction to our fight against diseases such as tuberculosis, leprosy, and kala-azar. The ICMR has also played a significant role in shaping our national health programs. During the COVID-19 pandemic, it established a nationwide testing network in record time and partnered in the development of India’s first indigenous COVID-19 vaccine. She expressed confidence that the ICMR is also taking effective measures toward the diagnosis of diseases like dengue.

President said that the occasion of a golden jubilee is not only a time to reflect upon and take pride in past achievements, but also an opportunity to set decisive goals for the future. We are moving forward with the objective of building Viksit Bharat by 2047. Strong collaboration among research institutions, centres of technical and higher education, and the industrial sector is crucial for building a healthy and empowered India. Premier institutions like the ICMR can take the lead in fostering such collaboration. She expressed confidence that the ICMR and its affiliated institutions will contribute to achieving the health-related goals of Viksit Bharat through research, collaboration and innovation.

Click here to see President's speech in Hindi

item.title: NITI Aayog holds first National Workshop on “Leadership as a Mission” on the completion of 25 years of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi as Head of Government
item.dc:creator: NITI Aayog
item.description: NITI Aayog NITI Aayog holds first National Workshop on “Leadership as a Mission” on the completion of 25 years of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi as Head of Government Dr. P.K. Mishra, Principal Secretary to the Prime Minister, delivers inaugural keynote address at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi Posted On: 17 NOV 2026 2:46PM by PIB Delhi NITI Aayog organised the National Workshop on “Leadership as Mission” at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi today, to draw on the learnings from the twenty-five years of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi as Head of Government.…
item.content:encoded:
NITI Aayog
NITI Aayog holds first National Workshop on “Leadership as a Mission” on the completion of 25 years of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi as Head of Government
Dr. P.K. Mishra, Principal Secretary to the Prime Minister, delivers inaugural keynote address at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi
Posted On: 17 NOV 2026 2:46PM by PIB Delhi

NITI Aayog organised the National Workshop on “Leadership as Mission” at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi today, to draw on the learnings from the twenty-five years of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi as Head of Government. The Prime Minister assumed office as Chief Minister of Gujarat in October 2001 and as Prime Minister of India in May 2014 and has led the Government at the State and the Union levels without a break since then. Throughout this period, he has held public office as a mission of service. His description of himself as the Pradhan Sevak places the citizen at the centre of every office of government, and the principles of Antyodaya, Jan Bhagidari and Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas, Sabka Vishwas, Sabka Prayas have guided the direction of governance at both levels.

The workshop is the first in a series of five National Workshops. The deliberations and first-hand experiences shared during the series will be developed into case studies and learning material for civil services training institutes, educational institutions and universities. Over the course of the series, the learning from these twenty-five years will also be taken forward through research and teaching material that sets out directions for policy and administration in the years leading up to Viksit Bharat @2047.

More than 900 participants attended the workshop, of whom 250 took part directly in the deliberations. The participants included Secretaries and senior officers of the Union and State Governments, District Collectors of Aspirational Districts, students of educational institutions and universities, and community partners and beneficiaries of national flagship schemes. The proceedings are also streamed on the iGOT Karmayogi platform and at Central and State Administrative Training Institutes, enabling officers from across the country to participate in the programme.

The workshop commenced with the National Song and the National Anthem followed by welcome address by Shri Anurag Jain, Chief Executive Officer, NITI Aayog. He highlighted that the objective of this workshop is to document the learnings from 25 years of leadership of the Hon’ble Prime Minister and translate them into institutional knowledge for the future.

He outlined four key lessons from the leadership journey. First, purpose must take precedence over hierarchical position, shifting the focus from individual leadership to a shared collective mission. Second, service must replace command, with governance centred on reaching the last person in the queue. Third, intrinsic conviction builds resilience, enabling adversity to become an opportunity for societal transformation. And fourth, true empowerment must outlive individual leadership through strong institutions, capable teams and sustainable systems.

Shri Ashok Kumar Lahiri, Vice Chairman, NITI Aayog, delivered the opening remarks. He said, “The role of strong political and administrative leadership is crucial in driving India's development journey. The transformational vision of our Hon’ble Prime Minister, marks a significant shift in India's national aspiration to become Viksit by 2047, reflecting the country’s transition towards a developed, prosperous and globally competitive nation.”

He highlighted NITI Aayog's integrated roadmap for realising this ambition of building a USD 30-40 trillion economy by 2047, with a per capita income of USD 15,000-18,000, supported by sustained annual real GDP growth of 7-10%.

Delivering the inaugural keynote address, Dr. P. K. Mishra, Principal Secretary to the Prime Minister, said that “India’s governance journey has been marked by defining milestones that demonstrate the power of decisive leadership and the ability to translate vision into action. From swift response to the 2001 Kutch earthquake to the country’s coordinated response to the COVID-19 pandemic, from expanding India’s footprint in the global space economy to the transformative impact of Lakhpati Didi initiative, these actions reflect how strong political will, responsive administration and mission-driven governance can bring about meaningful change in people’s lives.”

Shri Uday Kotak, Founder, Kotak Mahindra Bank, said that “The leadership of Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, both as Chief Minister of Gujarat and subsequently as Prime Minister of India, has consistently recognised entrepreneurship as a key driver of economic growth and nation-building. The institutionalisation of support systems, strengthening of financial and entrepreneurial ecosystems, and the emergence of a vibrant start-up landscape reflect this commitment.”

Dr. R. Balasubramaniam, Member, NITI Aayog, explained the design and structure of the workshop. He stated that the workshop approaches leadership through the decisions and actions in which it becomes visible, with the day’s proceedings structured to move from experience to analysis and from analysis to practice. The proceedings followed five stages: Learn, Analyse, Reflect, Apply and Commit under which participants learnt from first-hand accounts of significant decisions, analysed them through deliberations involving government, academia and citizens, reflected on enduring practices of public leadership, applied the learning to challenges in their own work and committed to specific changes in their leadership practices. He added that the workshop seeks to build an Indian body of knowledge on public leadership, drawing on Indian decisions and institutions, which will shape the way civil servants are trained and the way they lead in the years towards Viksit Bharat 2047.

During the Leadership Moments session, four speakers shared first-hand accounts of key moments and the leadership lessons emerging from them.

Shri Rajeev Topno, Additional Chief Secretary and Principal Secretary, Health and Family Welfare Department, Government of Gujarat, spoke on the reconstruction of Kutch following the 2001 earthquake. He highlighted that, Kutch 2001 was not merely a story of restoring normalcy, it was a story of creating a new normal through Jan Bhagidari, institutional strength and collective resolve. The experience highlighted four key pillars of effective governance, clarity and decisiveness in vision, solidarity and commitment, people’s participation with State support, and strong institution building.

Ms. Preeti Sudan, former Union Health Secretary and former Chairman, UPSC and former Member, Independent Panel for Pandemic Preparedness and Response, emphasised that under the leadership of Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, India’s COVID-19 response evolved from a whole-of-government approach into a whole-of-society movement. With the safety of doctors, nurses and frontline warriors prioritised, technology as its backbone, and Jan Andolan driving public participation, India mounted a coordinated response. Through Vaccine Maitri, the country further extended its commitment to global solidarity, supplying approximately 300 million vaccine doses to over 100 countries.

Shri Shailesh Kumar Singh, former Secretary, Ministry of Rural Development, Government of India said that “The Lakhpati Didi initiative is an example of how a vision can be translated into action at an unprecedented scale. The Hon’ble Prime Minister recognised rural women as entrepreneurs, producers and service providers, giving the initiative a clear and ambitious goal. Lakhpati Didi initiative goes beyond income generation, it is about fostering economic independence, dignity and recognition for women within their families and society. That, to me, is its larger purpose.”

Dr. S. Somanath, former Chairman, ISRO and former Secretary, Department of Space, Government of India, highlighted how liberalised FDI norms have opened new avenues for private sector participation, enabling space to emerge as a significant contributor to the economy. He emphasized that ISRO is playing a crucial role in facilitating this transition by extending its expertise, infrastructure and facilities to private players. Looking ahead, India’s Space Vision 2047, will further advance our scientific capabilities and strengthen India's position as a global space power.

Following the session, participants took part in the Case Clinic, where each group examined a specific decision from its assigned episode. Each group comprised of government officers, community partners and students, and was guided by a case writer trained under the Amrit Gyaan Kosh initiative of the Capacity Building Commission. The group deliberations, together with the first-hand accounts shared by the speakers, will be developed into case studies by the Capacity Building Commission and made available on the iGOT Karmayogi platform for use by civil servants, training institutions and universities.

Later in the day, a panel discussion on “Leadership for Viksit Bharat” will be held and government officers will take part in the Application Clinic. Dr. T.V. Somanathan, Cabinet Secretary, will launch the Karmayogi Sankalpa and deliver the closing remarks.

***

MJPS/PRK
